Alrighty then. Aftersun... it's nothing much. Sure, it's tender a little psychological but there's not much worth digging into here. It's a solemn, minimal film; very few characters, brief interactions and a hazy, dream-like presentation. The whole thing plays out like a distant memory that, seemed happy once, but as you age, you see the sad undercurrents of it. Neat idea, but the execution was spacey and pretentious. Aftersun follows a recently divorced dad and his young daughter on vacation. He's depressed and doing his best to hide it from her. She is growing up, starting to feel attractions and is making real connections with other humans. As the vacation goes on, the daughter and father begin to relate to each other on a deeper level. That's it. Aftersun is good insofar as you relate to it. Most people my age on this site come from fucked up, divorced, miserable families so they have these decaying memories. They look back and realize when they started to realize the cracks. They remember discovering how flawed and broken their parents were; coming of age in a world of dysfunction. I can't really relate so this movie didn't have as much meaning for ol' D.W. The Rumsfelds have always been intact. For me, it was a plodding, gimmicky bore that should have just been a short film or something. I'll never forget the first time I saw my father cry... but that doesn't make this movie good. The characters were middling; mostly slates for the audience to project their sadness onto. Alot of the editing was stupid too, and only sometimes justified. I did like the cinematography and acting, though, Paul Mescal is promising and I have liked almost all of his theatrical performances thus far. Aftersun didn't hold much value for me. I felt like it wasted alot of time and tried to pull heartstrings. It had good focus and some intentionality but when all was said and done, I just kinda threw my hands up in frustration. Pithy abstraction, faux-cuteness, faint natalism, not for me. Two Mutzies and Odenkirk-grade singing

Words cannot fully describe just how disappointed I am that this film did not land for me. For the last sort of three to four years ‘ Aftersun’ has been talked about as one of the most successful directorial debuts ever, and in the same breath one of the most moving films of the decade yet, I’m utterly let down. There were only really a few scenes I was able to honestly resonate with and I don’t believe Charlotte Wells completely unlocks the deeply personal and stagnant emotionality she desires. Fairly dissatisfied with Paul Mescal’s performance in the film too, in fact I feel as though Frankie Corio even outperformed the then 26-year-old which is shocking. It also completely derailed any nuanced meaning for me because the way he acts is a causality and emotional anchor for Corio’s character, so for him to then not prevail in the role was an immediate disaster. I hope that this improves on rewatch, granted I give it a second chance, although I don’t see that being super likely.

“Que pensabas que harías hoy cuando tenias 11?” Aftersun es una película que tenia guardada hace bastante tiempo, gente variada me la recomendaba porque parecía ser un film bastante crudo en cuanto a la relación parental y en simples palabras tocaba el corazón y te hacia llorar… no me pasó. Me parece interesante y precioso en verdad como la imagen y la paleta de colores que se ocupa te transporta realmente a la pre-adolescencia/niñez que Sophie concierne, me sentí en todo momento como si yo también conectara con mi niño interior. Sin embargo, creo que espere en toda la película a que sucediera algo sorprendente o que turnara la trama a algo más denso, a algo que me deje nervioso, o sea si, se logra, sobre todo ad portas del final de la película cuando la relación entre Sophie y Calum parece quebrarse la noche de su cumpleaños, pero sin más, se me hizo demasiado pretensiosa y lenta, es una trama tierna y triste, sobre todo por Paul Mescal interpretando a este padre que parece estar depresivo. Acotar que, aunque se me hizo esperable el que no se volverían a ver, fue un sentimiento ingenuo de pena el que la película finalice con quizás los recuerdos de la mini cámara de Sophie sobre las mejores vacaciones de su vida. Quizás no entendí el film, quizás no es mi tipo de genero al cual recurro para disfrutar, realmente la quería disfrutar pero simplemente no me llego… Cerrando, me parece increíble leer los comentarios sobre esta película, muchos de ellos replanteando la relación que cada individuo tiene con sus padres, porque si, la trama te hace replantearte, de forma implícita, sobre todo aquellas personas con padres separados, y en un punto sentí, que los roles se invertían, el padre parecía un niño y la hija la madre, muchas de las realidades pasadas y contemporáneas, en donde los hijos deben ser adultos responsables a temprana edad (y quizás, solo quizás, por eso Sophie se nos muestra como una niña de 11 que intenta entender la vida [un tanto arriesgada, incontrolable y placentera de la mayoría de edad]).

J'ai trouvé le film très lent et il manque, selon moi, de dynamisme. Pendant une grande partie du film, j'ai eu du mal à être réellement captivé, la seule scène qui m'a vraiment marqué est la séquence finale, lorsque le père et sa fille dansent ensemble avant la fin de leurs vacances. Les flashbacks qui s'entremêlent à ce moment donnent enfin tout son sens au film et apportent une forte charge émotionnelle. Le film montre avec beaucoup de subtilité comment le père cache sa souffrance pour préserver sa fille. En apparence, il essaie de lui offrir de belles vacances, mais on comprend qu'au fond il est profondément triste et terriblement seul. Il est père célibataire, confronté à des difficultés financières et sans véritable entourage, il porte un mal-être qu'il ne parvient plus à surmonter. La fin révèle également que l'on suivait en réalité les souvenirs de Sophie devenue adulte. Avec le recul, elle comprend enfin les signes qu'elle n'avait pas vus enfant et réalise à quel point son père allait mal avant son décès. Même si je n'ai pas été emballé par le rythme du film, je reconnais que cette conclusion est particulièrement touchante et donne une autre dimension a l’histoire .

Aftersun is one of those films that feels incredibly simple on the surface, yet completely devastating underneath. The performances are so natural that they never feel like acting, they feel like real people, which makes the relationship between Sophie and her dad (Callum) deeply personal and relatable. That ordinary, everyday quality is what makes the film so heartbreaking, because it captures the small moments we often overlook until they become memories. Rather than relying on dramatic events, Aftersun quietly builds an emotional weight that lingers long after it ends, leaving a sense of love, loss and regret that feels painfully human.

This was a movie which i didnt understand and definitely need to rewatch. Incredible acting from Mescal and Corio. Was clearly a movie which leans heavily on the bond between father and daughter and deals with the crippling depression which Mescal's character tries to hide from his daughter, Sophie. From the first sort of 20 minutes, you can tell that this film is showing and not telling , whether it's the very long shots focused on a single subject, or the use of solemn and dark composed music for the film within moments which do not warrant it, the film portrays depression in a much more subconscious way than ive seen other films and series manage. The use of the rave scenes, and lingering shots on what seems like random subjects are something I should analyse on a rewatch, as I am no film buff and therefore have not been able to pick up on the purpose of these scenes and what the intention of the cinematography is very well. The consistently sinister or sombre music being draped over the scenes in this film is representative of how depression consumes every waking minute of a person's life. I believe there was also a theme of a young person being introduced to the world of romance and sexual exploration, with lingering shots of teenagers kissing whilst Sophie was nearby, or that one scene of her overhearing some teenagers talking about a sexual experience. I initially assumed that the sinister and sombre music being used during these scenes was to represent how a young individual's introduction to sexual experiences from others educating said person could represent grooming. However upon research for this film's meaning, I found that this might not be the case? Sex as a theme isnt really a topic discussed online (or at least on reddit) So perhaps for that reason I dont think these scenes are about grooming but rather the coming-of-age experience of discovering romance, love and sex as an additional theme ALONGSIDE the depression Sophie's dad suffers from? If it's not clear, I havent fully understood what this movie is actually about. To really get a better understanding of the film I should rewatch it probably. I liked this film a lot, but oh wow I was very confused.

Ok, so this took a lot of thinking, but I think I finally made sense of this film. This film made me see that you only know the version of someone that they show to you. The memories you have with or of someone are probably not actually what happened or who they truly are and felt in those moments. Our memories, especially from childhood can often have a rose coloured lense over them because at that time, you weren't aware of things in the grand scheme. You had an innocent mind because you were a kid. Most of my personal childhood memories have gaps. These gaps could have been good events or not so good events, and I'll never know because there was no camera. My siblings probably share the same memories as me, but with less or more gaps, with different details and specifics. My parents probably remember every specific and have no gaps in the memories I have from being a kid. Its like we were all there, at the same event, where we experienced the same thing, but we all probably remember it a little bit different. I probably won't remember writing this review, the same way I don't remember writing most of my reviews after a few weeks. Memory is a weird thing when you think about it. And this movie really made me think about it.

Te enseña que la vida es incluso irónica de una manera tan particular y nostálgica. Es una obra de arte genuina, real, cruda... pero sin dejar de ser extremadamente cuidada y linda. Dirigida de manera excepcional, te deja una marca en el corazón.

“You can live wherever you want to live. Be whoever you want to be. You have time." I used to envy people who had a documented life when they were kids, pictures and videos of them living as if it was the proof of existence. To see them through the eyes of their parents on how much they love and care enough to capture those moments, something to look back on in the future. I think it stems from my hatred and shame that every time there is an activity in school that requires baby photos, I will always be the only one worrying, for I have nothing to show. Maybe it was due to poverty? Lack of love and attention? Maybe they don’t just see the point in taking photos? Or maybe a little bit of a mix of all? It kinda felt bitter and pathetic, just a child wondering why I am the only one in the room who lacks that experience…and weirdly enough, I would find myself imagining that I am the one in other children's shoes, fantasizing about what it feels like to be in their family? Throughout the movie I just kept on thinking and reflecting about my relationship with my Papa. Initially I had this realization that I’ve never had anything that I could look back to; we barely had any pictures nor memories since we never went on vacations, went on a trip, or even simply went out. But I thought it would be an awesome thing to do so…I do think he deserves to have fun and do trivial things and see life without always being in a survival mode worrying about spending money on what seems to fit in the ‘wants’ and not ‘need’ category. I’ve spent most of my life with him, and I think personality-wise I am more like him. I might not like him as a person with some of his questionable morals and beliefs, but I could pretty much say that he was a great dad who literally did everything just so that me and my brother doesn't have to worry going on an empty stomach and even provide things that might not be grand, but it was better than having nothing. Actually, I do think that my dad is a cool person; he experienced so much hardship in life and knows a lot of skills in order to survive. I sometimes wish that I knew him better or even bonded with him with life outside of the house. Other times, I imagine what would his life be if I hadn't existed? The sole reason why I want to succeed in life, to have money, is just to spoil them and return all the hard work they've put in raising me; growing up, I think my parents value money more than anything, and I do get why, so I thought that maybe giving back with money would be the best thing they would totally appreciate—so that they could finally live the life for themselves and experience what they truly deserve: pampering their own needs and not for the sake of other people.

This film felt like watching a Polaroid develop, so when we get to the scene with the photo on the table, the image of Calum and Sophie coming into focus, it felt perfect. That’s what it’s like though, to look back onto our childhoods, the image of our parents shifting over time. This one was a brutal gut punch. The moment when Sophie buries her face into Calum’s chest as they dance completely broke me.

i just feel hollow, a slow melancholic dream with the highest highs and the lowest lows. it’s a fathers desperate attempts to create a happy memory for his daughter, young Sophie believes they’re both underneath the same sky. that’s the most heart breaking thing about this movie, scenes of Calum alone imagined by the adult Sophie to be so broken, sobbing furiously in his bedroom, his mask stripped by so many mentally and physically, it’s torturous. the experience of reliving her childhood memory now with adult sensibility, finding out what her father was through, must be devastating. the last dance, knowing its his last dance. the walk into the sea, tai chi on the balcony, big lavish purchase of £800 rug for Sophie that she said he can’t afford. gut wrenching.

I sat down and watched this twice consecutively tonight. I think part of the beauty of this film is that it takes a minute to get. it’s very beautiful and visually impressive, but the deeper meaning is definitely supposed to be lost to you on your first viewing, seeing as the whole thing happens in Sophie’s imagination. you are living it through her as she tries to piece together her memories of the trip and who her father really was. the symbolism here is insane. there’s definitely more to unpack, but the two that stood out to me were the “rave” scenes being a metaphor for Sophie’s incomplete memories of Calum, and the polaroid photograph that sort of made the movie’s meaning click for me: that the physical media is really all Soph can see when she delves back into her old memories. on my first viewing I didn’t really get it until that moment - I just thought it was very pretty and was unsettled by how clearly disturbed Calum was on his own. but the second time around I cried. this is perfect and takes levels of understanding, which is exactly what I look for in a movie.

It’s fun to try to figure things out, interpret what’s happening, and come up with theories. You’re given plenty of time to do so, too, since some conversations are long and some shots are even longer. For me, it all dragged on a bit too much and ended unsatisfactorily. c’est un film très lent, avec une atmosphère étrange et de très très très très longs dialogues. c’est un infini procès, avec une embrouille interminable, qui révèle une ambiance très sombre et des personnages tous plus bizarres les uns que les autres. on comprend pas tout et c’est très compliqué d’accrocher. certains plans sont filmées de façon original, et les scènes sont vraiment longues. c’est un film chargé en émotion, avec beaucoup de secrets enfouies. au bout d’un moment ça devient vraiment interminable, des faits surgissent, des hypothèses sont conjecturées, mais c’est jamais explicitement concret. bon ok la façon dont c’est réalisé est très intéressante. par contre, j’ai carrément détesté la fin, pcq tout le long on s’attend à une réponse concrète mais le but du film c’est justement de ne donner aucune réponse, du coup c’est super frustrant. toute l’histoire on peut l’interpréter seulement par des « peut être » et jamais par de véritables faits. chacun des personnages sont intéressants, avec des points de vus différents et des façons de subir la situation différentes, mais le spectateur est à la place des jurés, donc c’est très compliqué de savoir démêlé le vrai du faux. le film rappelle que le verdict ne coïncide pas forcément avec la vérité, et les hypothèses de la potentielle vérité restent plausible. cependant le lien avec le titre du film est très pertinent, en montrant la chute de chacun des personnages de façon disséquées. bon, en toute honnêteté je n’ai pas aimé. le fond du film est émouvant et bien recherché. MAIS, c’est lent + dialogues interminables + bcp de choses abstraites et surtout surtout surtout le film répond à rien, ça te laisse sur ta fin, c’est à toi d’interpréter et de trouver la vérité, la fin est ouverte et ne répond à aucune questions que tu te poses durant tout le film. c’est frustrant et c’est carrément ce que je n’aime pas.

J’en avais énormément entendu parler en bien, et certains le considèrent même comme un chef-d’œuvre. On me l’avait vraiment vendu comme un film incroyable, donc forcément, j’en attendais beaucoup. Et honnêtement, j’ai été assez déçu. Je comprend ce que dénonce le film et ce qu'il reflète de notre société et de la justice. Cependant j'ai trouvé ça long. Ce qui me gêne avec ce film c'est le côté élitiste de la communauté, comme si le fait de ne pas avoir une fin clairement expliquée rendait automatiquement le film plus intelligent. Personnellement, je trouve que ça peut vite donner une certaine prétention au film et à la manière dont il est présenté. Le fait de laisser le spectateur interpréter la fin peut être intéressant, mais ça ne signifie pas forcément que le film est meilleur ou plus intelligent. En soi, ça reste un bon film, je ne vais pas dire le contraire. Mais je pense que le principal problème, c’est que dès qu’un film sort un peu de l’ordinaire et propose quelque chose d’original, les gens ont tendance à énormément s’emballer. On lui attribue tout de suite une dimension exceptionnelle, voire de chef-d'œuvre. C'est dommage mais ça reste un bon film.

Mettez du respect et de la lumière sur le cinéma féminin. Un film de procès qui ne cherche jamais vraiment le verdict, mais la faille. Triet construit son récit comme une dissection minutieuse du couple, où chaque certitude s'effrite à mesure que le tribunal (et le spectateur) croit avancer. Sandra Hüller y est habitée d'une opacité fascinante : on ne sait jamais si son intelligence est une armure ou un aveu. Mais au-delà du dispositif judiciaire, c'est une question bien plus vertigineuse que pose le film : connaît-on vraiment l'autre ? Son voisin, son frère, sa sœur, son ou sa compagne ? Aucune famille n'échappe aux secrets de polichinelle, à ces zones d'ombre qui persistent sans jamais être nommées. Chaque foyer a ses casseroles, ses non-dits tolérés en silence. C'est ce qui rend le film aussi dramatique que profondément humain. Il ne s'agit pas de juger un couple, mais de mesurer combien la connaissance intime de l'autre [ et de soi-même ] reste toujours partielle, négociée, parfois illusoire. Une leçon d'humilité face à la complexité des êtres. La mise en scène, souvent austère, presque clinique, épouse cette froideur alpine du chalet, comme si le décor lui-même refusait de trancher. C'est là toute l'ambiguïté du film : il ne raconte pas une mort mais l'impossibilité de connaître véritablement l'autre même après des années de vie commune. Les 2h30 pèsent par moments, notamment dans les longueurs procédurales qui, même si elles nourrissent le vertige du doute, testent aussi la patience. L'usage de l'anglais, pivot thématique plus que coquetterie, dérange certains. J'avoue que j'ai eu du mal avec ce yoyo entre les langues mais c'est à tort selon moi, tant il matérialise la distance entre les langues, les cultures, et finalement entre les personnes elles-mêmes. Une Palme d'or qui ne fait pas l'unanimité, et c'est peut-être normal. le film refuse lui-même toute unanimité sur ce qu'il raconte comme il refuse toute certitude sur ceux qu'on croit connaître. Pas le meilleur rythme mais très bon film.

Palme d’or 2023 et couronné de nombreuses récompenses, Anatomie d’une chute de Justine Triet mérite largement sa réputation. Derrière son apparence de film judiciaire se cache avant tout une dissection fascinante d’un couple en crise, où chaque détail du quotidien prend une importance capitale. Le suspense autour de ce whodunit atypique fonctionne parfaitement, mais le véritable sujet est ailleurs : les ressentis, les incompréhensions et les visions opposées que deux personnes peuvent avoir d’une même histoire. Sandra Hüller livre une prestation remarquable, parvenant à transmettre une multitude d’émotions d’un simple regard. Une réalisation subtile qui nous plonge au plus près des émotions des personnages. Un très bon film.

From the jump this movie’s sound design and framing are next level. Just truly stunning work. As is befitting the French. They don’t do much super well but, boy, can they make movies. There’s something inherently cinematic about the French language. It lends itself to the dramatic. This movie has one of the best openings I have ever seen. Ratcheting up the tension immediately. In particular, a lingering shot on the guide dog of the half blind kid is astounding. The performances in this movie are all fantastic. Funny though, the DOG is the best actor in the movie! You love to see it. The drama brought on by the incompetence (at best) or clear corruption and railroading (at worst) of the French police is infuriating. Especially when you learn that this was inspired by a real case that the Italian police fumbled hard as hell. I love courtroom/crime dramas and this movie is a masterclass in the genre. Highly recommend.

bir köpek var filmde, hani al tüm oyunculuk ödüllerini ona ver inanılmaz iyi oynamış. Bir sabaha açılıyor film, bir aile. Anne, baba ve çocuk. Çocuğumuz görme engelli, Annemiz sahnede son derece sıcak fakat babamız öyle mesafeli ki kadraja girmeye bile yeltenmiyor. Sadece açtığı müziğin sesiyle varlığından haberdar ediyor bizi. Bu tanıtımdan sonra, bir düşüş gerçekleşiyor. Çocuğumuz evde değilken, baba pencereden düşüp ölüyor. O sırada evde bulunan tek kişi olan Anne ise ileride gerçekleşecek duruşmaların baş şüphelisi konumuna geçiyor. Daha sonra, filmimiz ilerledikçe bu düşüşü derinlemesine analiz ediyor, bir bakıma anatomisini çıkarıyor. Bu düşüş yalnızca  ölüme yol açmış bu kaza/cinayetin değil; bir aşkın, bir ailenin ve en önemlisi kişilere dair kafamızda oluşturduğumuz portrelerin de düşüşü. Onlara atfettiğimiz her bir iyi özelliğin, birlikte yaşadığımız her bir güzel anının bambaşka bir bağlamda nasıl bir silaha, korkunç bir eylemin kanıtına dönüşebileceğinin anatomisi. İşte bu film, tam olarak bununla ilgileniyor. İki saat otuz dakika boyunca filmimiz bunu anlatıyor. Gerçekte ne oldu? Aslında daha doğrusu, gerçekte ne olduğunu düşünüyorsun? Bu soru, izleyiciye düzenli olarak soruluyor ve  verdiğimiz cevaplar çoğu zaman (en azından benim verdiğim) bir öncekinden farklı oluyor. Spoiler olmayacak merak etmeyin, sadece ufak bir sahneden örnek vermek istiyorum. Bana kalırsa film başlangıçta sıkıca annemizin perspektifinden ilerliyor. Ortam onun açısından kuruluyor, onun gözlerinden şahit oluyoruz. Haliyle çoğumuz bu davada Annemin tarafını tutmuş oluyor. Sonra duruşmalar başlıyor ve bir sabah bir ses kaydı dinliyoruz. Ses kaydı bir tartışma hakkında. Önce ufak gerginlikler çıkıyor, sonra saygının sürdürüldüğü bir tartışmaya dönüyor. Fakat ne zamanki bu tartışma fiziksel şiddetin de dahil olduğu bir kavgaya dönüyor, görüntü kesiliyor ve aynı karakterlerimiz gibi sadece ses kaydıyla tanık oluyoruz geçmişe. Burada artık ne olduğunun kararı bize düşüyor. Ve o ana kadar her zaman tek bir açıya güvenmiş olan biz, kendimizi şüphe ederken buluyoruz. Film, bu tarafsız anlatımını soğuk atmosferi ve karakterlere mesafeli duruşuyla güçlendirmiş. Aynı zamanda ara ara kameranın el çekimi, handheld bir tarza geçmesiyle de sizi olan olayların içine bırakıyor. Kimi zaman kamera yaşananlara ayak uyduramıyor, sahne pozlamasında hatalara yer veriyor ve olanları olduğu gibi sergilemekte başarısız oluyor. Bu sayede anlattığı temayı da ustalıkla desteklemiş oluyor. Oyunculuklar gerçekten de efsane. Yazdığım birçok incelemede oyunculukları övüyorum, ben de bunun farkındayım. Fakat bana sorsanız en iyi oyunculuklar hangi filmdeydi diye, şüphe bile etmeden Anatomy of a Fall derdim. Sandra Hüller, kendi ana dili olmayan iki dilde konuşmasına rağmen destansı bir performans vermiş. Milo Machado-Graner unutulmaz bir oyunculuk sergilemiş. Hem çocuk oyuncu, hem görme engelli bir karakter hem de yas sürecini anlatan senaryo. Aktörümüz aleyhine olabilecek tüm durumların üstesinden ustalıkla gelmiş. Kadrodaki diğer oyuncularsa ortalamın çok üstünde performanslar vererek bu iki başrolümüzün emeğini boşa çıkarmamış. Son olarak, filmi sıkıcı bulan insanların olduğunun farkındayım. Hatta bunlardan birisi ablam. Dürüst konuşmam gerekirse beni bir an bile sıkmadı. Hatta film beni içine almakta o kadar başarılıydı ki bir sahnede karakterin sigarasından gelen dumanın benim odamda dolaştığını sandım. Zevk meselesidir diyip filmin temposu hakkındaki kararı size bırakıyorum. Benim için kusursuza çok yakın bir filmdi. Duygusal bağ kurmakta zorlanmış olsam da bunun bir sonraki izleyişimlerimde gerçekleşebileceğine hâlâ daha inanıyorum. Ayrıca, bir noktada bu duruma bilerek yapıldığını düşündüğümden çok da büyük bir problem olarak bakamıyorum. Şiddetle tavsiye ediyorum.

As the end marker for a long running generation of marvel movies, Endgame unfortunately drops the ball in all ways that matter. A lame attempt at reconciling irreversible character and wider plot choices, this film not only disrupts long established character growth and progression, but it also abruptly cuts off any opportunity for what many would call a “happy ending.” Multiple beloved characters are given the “tortured male existence trope,” wherein their wider personality and moral identity are swept to the wayside in order to justify a new generation of characters to swoop in following their exit. For example, by both butchering Peggy Carter and Steve Rogers emotional maturation and individuality in order to manufacture a “romantic reunification” following Steve’s travel back in time, Marvel has essentially removed both Peggy’s autonomy outside of being “Captain Americas love interest,” as well as Steve’s long established faithfulness to Bucky Barnes and his dedication to serving the weak. In no world would Steve rogers abandon a freshly reintroduced to society Bucky, nor a disrupted world reeling with the sudden re-appearance of 50% of the world’s population. In his decision to abandon his shield and interrupt Peggy’s progression towards an accomplished life as a shield founder and agent, as well as her pursuit of future love and motherhood as expressed in the original timeline, Steve is making an exceptionally selfish decision—which as any Marvel fan is aware—is the antithesis of his character. This is just one of the irreconcilable changes made to a central character that insults years of character establishment and development, which is then followed by yet again a female character being fridged for the greater plot. First starting with Gamora in Infinity war and now Natasha in Endgame, it is clear to see that the writers find no use for these strong female characters in these last plot stages other than as a motivation for male suffering and lament. Gamora, both present and past iterations of herself (as featured in this film), have much more worth as a character representing long building abusive deprogramming and female strength and endurance in the face of tragedy, than as a “sad she’s different than my girlfriend” trope—as presented by Peter Quills reaction to her appearance. Prior to this, viewers are slapped in the face with the sacrifice of Natasha for the soul stone, where her death is framed as a noble sacrifice in order to allow Clint Barton to return to his family once the snap is reversed. While faithful to Natasha’s character, one can only reconcile so much with the fact that it had to be only female character of the original Avengers to lose her life first. This is especially exasperated by the emphasized female power scene in the final battle, where every female hero on scene band together to fight, almost as an attempt by the writers to apologize for killing off the woman who pioneered female superhero-dom in modern media not 40 minutes earlier. All in all, these are just some of the many faults within this movie—which in its essence is a blatant attempt to slap a crooked bandaid on Marvels obvious (and clumsy) transition to a newer generation of actors and characters. As entertaining as a battle packed, time travel action movie can be, Avengers Endgame is a lazy attempt at hopefully pushing viewers towards future projects as they kill off their favorite characters one by one. We can only hope that these new superhero’s will be given the opportunity to grow into characters of their own and establish a storyline outside of the shadow of their predecessors.

Ouais. Ok. Cool. Franchement ce film a cette note car c'est un film charnière, sinon je lui aurais mis 2 étoiles en terme de kiffe. Je n'ai ressenti aucune émotions, cela ne m'a pas fait rire et je n'étais pas ébahi ni ému. Le début est sympathique, voir Thor gros alcoolo c'est étrange, de même voir Tony Stark avec un enfant m'a surpris, mais c'est tout. Déjà je n'apprécie pas le fait de remonter le temps à l'aide de la technologique quantique. Ensuite je ne pense pas que les pierres permettent de refermer la branche d'univers créée (donc il existe trois univers distincts, le premier est celui dans lequel l'histoire se passe, le second est celui dans lequel on a prit les pierres et le dernier est celui dans lequel on a pris les pierres puis on les a restitués). Enfin Steve Rogers devrait avoir plus de 100 ans donc comment est-il en vie à la fin pour transmettre le costume et le bouclier ?? Cela étant dit c'était sympathique de revenir dans les précédents films, mais bon moi ce ne m'a pas trop touché vu que je les ai vu pour la plupart il y a moins de dix jours. Captain America est symbole et non un super-héros classique, il représente l'Amérique mais aussi la loyauté, le courage, le charisme, il est donc impersonnel et tout le monde qui est en digne peut être Captain America, c'est pour cela que je ne suis pas gêné par le fait que Steve Rogers ne soit plus Captain America à présent. D'ailleurs en parlant de dignité, j'ai trouve ça hyper classe que Steve Rogers ait pu maîtriser Mjöllnir. J'ai trop le seum que Black Widow soit morte c'est une de mes préférées. Elle aurait dû être présente pour l'une des meilleurs scènes du film : Toutes les super-héroïnes combattant côte à côte. La scène du sacrifice entre Hawkeye et Black Widow est bien je trouve et aussi un peu émouvante. Je suis pas content que Captain Marvel n'ait pas fait grand chose, je pense qu'elle peut prendre Thanos en 1v1 facile et c'est bien la seule. Dans mon classement elle est deuxième devant Wanda et derrière Doctor Strange. J'ai bien aimé aussi que l'Ancien soit présente pour défendre la Terre lorsque Loki était de mèche avec Ronan. J'apprécie le geste héroïque de Tony Stark qui fait subir à Thanos ce qu'il a fait subir à la moitié des êtres vivants. J'aime bien quand Thor et Peter se lancent dans une guerre d'egros (parce qu'ils ont tous les deux un énorme ego et qu'ils sont gros, hehehehehehehe je suis très fier et je souris bêtement derrière l'écran). Il y a une dernière question que je me pose du coup, dans l'histoire on est en 2019 ou bien 2024, ceux qui sont restés vivants ont vieillis par conséquent tous les élèves du lycée de Peter Parker sont morts parce que sinon certains auraient fini leurs études. Bon on verra bien parce que j'ai pas vu Spider-Man : Far from Home. Papa a répondu à une des mes contestations Captain America est encore vivant car il n'est plus un homme normal (ça fait sens). Bref le film ne m'a pas enthousiasmé. Après avoir réfléchi durant la nuit je compte au moins 9 univers parallèle, l'originel puis 4 paires d'univers (car les pierres ont été empruntés à des années différentes) constitué de la manière suivante : un univers dans lequel la pierre n'est plus puis un autre où la pierre n'était plus avant qu'elle ne soit restituée. Mais du coup ces univers dans lesquels rien ne semble avoir changer possède le même futur que l'original et du coup cela créer infiniment des univers parallèles. Donc maintenant on ne sait pas si nous sommes dans l'univers originel ou dans une des répliques (peut-être que je me trompe et qu'il y a une faille dans mon raisonnement). Du coup même si Rogers avait la capacité de vivre plus de 100 ans, il ne devrait pas être dans cette timeline et n'aurait pas donc pu transmettre son rôle. Vu le 06/08/2026

Siguiente paso en la maratón Marvelita para estar un poco al día pre-Spiderman. Bastante sorprendido con que así sea el clímax final de 22 películas, porque realmente Infinity War sí se siente como tal y Endgame solo cumple la última hora y quizá en su planteamiento inicial. El histórico final de la anterior continua con un mundo casi post apocalíptico que me hubiera encantado que se explotara un pelín más. Tras ese inicio, la película claramente tiene el objetivo de llegar a una batalla final épica y falla clamorosamente en la manera de lograrlo. El planteamiento argumental es hacer viajes en el tiempo para robar las gemas del infinito, usarlas para revivir a todo el mundo y devolverlas a su lugar correspondiente para no generar líneas temporales caóticas. A las paradojas propias de las pelis de viajes en el tiempo no se le presta excesiva atención porque tampoco es el sitio, y así se permiten darle alguna patadita a la lógica. Eso funciona como excusa para hacer una especie de repaso a algunas pelis y personajes que se siente un poco liosa, anti climática y de una autorreferencialidad  que juega en contra de la épica de la peli. Esa vuelta a espacios de pelis anteriores sirve como excusa para traer a Thanos (el de la línea temporal actual está muerto) de vuelta, mucho menos desarrollado e interesante que la anterior. Además, lo más grave, es poco consistente con lo ocurrido ya que el personaje parece reaccionar a cosas que él no ha vivido. Por ejemplo, critica a los humanos por no haber sabido aprovechar su plan y por ello los condena a desaparecer para crear un nuevo mundo de cero. No queda natural y parece mucho más villano básico que en la anterior. La última hora vuelve a ser increíble, la batalla final es espectacular y el final con el sacrificio de Iron Man (que inició el MCU y acabó con él hasta ese momento) es muy emotivo.

Honestly, upon rewatching these movies, as decade-defining as it was to see the Avengers movies in theaters, they just don't hit the same on home release. Like they're plenty entertaining, and Infinity War is genuinely a great movie, but the payoff and subsequent downward trend of the MCU movies that directly followed this one (which has recently gotten better with additions like the last 2 Spider-Man movies and Thunderbolts) just feels a bit exhausting rewatching this one. I think this more negative approach I'm having with this rewatch stems from the anxiety of the upcoming Avengers movie being centered around my favorite comic book character of all time, Dr Doom, who is miles more powerful and methodical than a character like Thanos. As well as the MCU's portrayal of the character was, Thanos could and should never hold a candle. Before the MCU was celebrated for giving a new life and dedicated following to all the B-list characters Marvel had to settle with due to the big 3 (Spider-Man, F4, and the X-Men) being owned by Fox and Sony, there was a legacy of iconic comic heroes and villains that spanned over half a decade. And within the culture of comics, if you asked someone to name a comic book villain from Marvel Comics, 9/10 you're not going to hear Thanos, Ultron, or even Venom. They will say Dr. Doom. To the comic fan, Thanos is a nice can of RC Cola, but Doom... Doom is Coke from a glass. Despite this level of hype this character is known for, his film adaptations have been genuinely terrible, to the point of being disrespectful (I'm looking at you F4 2016). After being completely blown away by Infinity War , I have to say I’ve been left feeling a little bit disappointed in the saga’s conclusion. Infinity War is very well structured and executes all the beats it needs to hit to deliver something I felt was original and emotionally satisfying. Half of the universe’s population is gone, along with half of the heroes we love, and we’re left feeling hopeless, just like them. This is something we carry with us into the first 30 minutes of Endgame , which again subverted my expectations (positively) and dug the hole of wondering how they’d resolve this even deeper. When then, probably not even 10 minutes later, fucking time travel is thrown out there, it feels incredibly cheap. Instead of carrying the great momentum from the previous film, it becomes, from then on, a kids’ movie. Instead of the events leading the story, which I think made Infinity War so refreshing, it feels predictable, like the events are just following a path that will ultimately end in Marvel getting that big ensemble battle scene they wanted. From the moment time travel was mentioned, all the stakes disappeared. Though I don’t think it was done terribly, and it sets up the multiverse stuff in a good manner. Big spoilers if you somehow don’t know this, but Iron Man’s death hit me way less than I thought it would. Maybe it’s because I already knew it would happen. Maybe it’s because I didn’t watch every Iron Man film in theaters since they first started coming out. But still, I feel like a well-executed death should still do more for me emotionally, especially for a character of such significance. I think, along with a lot of what happens in this film, it was rushed. Yes, it had been foreshadowed—well, at that—but to me it felt like Marvel just thought, «Well, someone has to die. Who would make the most people cry?» And because it’s Iron Man, and Iron Man is Robert Downey Jr., they can just bring him back anyway, and people will eat it up. I don’t like what they did with Thor either. That is not the same fucking guy we saw being willing to give everything to save Asgard. I think Marvel dug themselves into a hole they hadn’t planned a way to get out of, which in the end makes for an overstuffed and rushed saga finale. Like Infinity War , it’s not particularly pretty to look at either, but now without the storytelling chops to make me look past most of it. I think it WOULD be a good film if it were written with a little more thought. Dangerously close to giving this 3 stars. It could easily be split into two films, honestly. It’s 5am now. I have more to say but can’t form any more thoughts. Good night . And bye MCU (for a bit) gonna watch Satantango now. Or dancing pig

" I love you 3000 ".                      "It's Been a Long, Long Time". El cierre definitivo de una era que cambió la historia del cine comercial para siempre. Después de 11 años, 22 películas y docenas de arcos argumentales entrelazados, Avengers: Endgame no solo logra estar a la altura de las colosales expectativas, sino que entrega una experiencia cinematográfica épica, nostálgica y profundamente emotiva. La película equilibra magistralmente la melancolía del duelo tras las pérdidas de Infinity War con la esperanza, la acción a escala monumental y el humor característico del UCM . El viaje en el tiempo no es solo un recurso narrativo, sino una hermosa carta de amor a toda la franquicia, permitiéndonos revivir momentos icónicos desde una nueva perspectiva antes del enfrentamiento final. El clímax y la batalla final es puro espectáculo visual y fan service ejecutado con brillantez, pero su verdadero corazón reside en las despedidas. Darle un cierre tan digno, humano y perfecto a personajes con los que crecimos — en especial a Tony Stark y Steve Rogers — es el mayor logro de los hermanos Russo. Un hito generacional que difícilmente se volverá a repetir. "Avengers... assemble." — Steve Rogers "I'm gonna need a dance raincheck."

Barbie wants to empower women while apparently believing women can’t understand subtext. I’m still trying to figure out who this movie is for. Kids are too young to understand most of what it’s trying to say about womanhood, sexism, beauty standards, motherhood, careers and social expectations. And adult women absolutely do not need a two-hour movie explaining to them that being a woman can be difficult. I’m apparently old enough to understand patriarchy but not old enough to recognize a metaphor without Margot Robbie explaining it to me. It wants to tell women they’re intelligent, strong and capable while simultaneously refusing to trust them to understand a theme unless someone delivers a monologue explaining exactly what it means. That irony might be the most interesting thing in the entire movie.

Enfin vu le film le plus populaire de Greta Gerwig (et mon premier film d’elle par ailleurs). Malheureusement j’ai pas été emballé par la proposition. On en fait trop d’ailleurs avec la musique durant tout le film c’est tellement fatiguant qu’un moment, il y a deux pistes musicales l’une sur l’autre c’est juste insupportable. Le côté monde alternatif, les côtés positifs et négatifs de Barbie avec ses stéréotypes sur le corps et l’esprit féminin, montrer qu’elle était, est et sera une figure de proue des jeunes filles mais surtout à l’avenir, une figure d’émancipation féminine dans une société patriarcale. The film is just as plastic and artificial as the source material it’s based on. I was severely disappointed after I finished the film. It has no nuance, no depth and for me, it’s just a vapid, virtue signaling mess. The problem isn’t the moral core of the film, which I do agree with, but how it’s dealt with. In my opinion it feels surface level and strangely disingenuous. This isn’t helped by the story, which has no twists and no particularly strong plot, it’s just filled with a bunch of underdeveloped characters that flash their fake smile at you as they wave the films message in your face like a great pink neon sign. That being said, the film has its moments, but most of these come from the more silly joke driven bits and are quickly overshadowed by the “I’m fourteen and this is deep” level existentialism. It’s like Gerwig was torn between making a film for young girls and a serious feminist film, and then from that inner battle rose this compromise, which fails to deliver on either. Still, thanks for all the silly goofs it’s not unbearable watch, at times it’s almost entertaining. Though, it’s a crime that the song Barbie Girl was not once played. Shame.

Un film qui m’a plutôt surpris par ce qu’il cherche à raconter derrière son apparence de comédie colorée et légère. Barbie est évidemment très drôle et possède une identité visuelle vraiment réussie. Les décors, les costumes et la direction artistique donnent au film une personnalité qu’on reconnaît immédiatement. Margot Robbie et Ryan Gosling sont également excellents, avec un Ryan Gosling qui vole presque la vedette à chacune de ses apparitions. J’ai surtout apprécié le fait que le film ne se contente pas de faire une simple adaptation de la poupée Barbie. Il aborde des sujets plus sérieux sur les attentes liées aux hommes et aux femmes, l’identité et la place qu’on cherche à trouver dans la société. Cependant, malgré toutes ses qualités, je n’ai pas été aussi touché que je l’aurais voulu. Certains messages sont parfois un peu trop appuyés et le film m’a semblé perdre un peu de son charme lorsqu’il devient plus sérieux. Une comédie originale, drôle et très bien réalisée, avec de bonnes idées et d’excellentes performances, mais qui ne m’aura pas totalement convaincu.

Greta Gerwig left subtlety and her serious face at the door for this one, and in the hands of a less capable cast and crew, it would probably fall apart. But what makes Barbie work is the absurdity and the cast and crew not taking things seriously. Ultimately, the issues it tackles are ridiculous one that really shouldn’t be issues anyway (equality, acceptance, etc.) and so making a movie that doesn’t take itself seriously and pokes fun at everything is the perfect way to tackle such absurdity. I think some people fell into the trap of trying to look below the surface of this movie, but with Barbie , what you see is what you get, and that is not at all a bad thing. I did have a couple issues with certain characters feeling a bit too flat and I thought the real world stuff was kinda boring, but overall I think this movie works really well and accomplishes all that it set out to do. Greta Gerwig is a really fantastic director and I very much look forward to her take on Narnia.

I was curious about this movie because of a ridiculously enticing trailer that had Leonard Cohen 's " You want it Darker " playing over it. The lyrics seemed perfect for the images I was seeing on screen : "There's a lover in the story, but the story's still the same - There's a lullaby for suffering and a paradox to blame - I didn't know I had permission to murder and to maim - You want it darker ? We kill the flame." Well, I wish I had never seen that trailer. Because, truly, nothing was remotely as good as what those 2 minutes teased and suggested. [Spoilers ahead] ( Before I start - I know that this is adapted from a book, and I've seen, as always, people say that the book was better, but know that I am not aware of the differences bewteen the original story and its adaptation.) THE PLOT : Against her father's rules, Maren, 18, sneaks out of the house to join a slumber party with 3 other girls. She must go back ' before 6AM ' she says, just in case. We barely have any time to get to know any character, our protagonist included, that she bites off her friend's finger. She comes back home, bloodied, banging on the front door. Her dad, instantly, gives her a " You didn't ", confirming this wasn't a first. " You have 3 minutes to pack before we leave and the police comes ". This clearly isn't a first. Maren and her father flee, and start a new life, all over again. But soon enough, her dad disappears. Maren is left all alone with her 'issue', with, as a goodbye, a message on a cassette to listen to, and a birth certificate with her estranged Mother's name. Here starts the girl's journey to find the latter, and herself alongside. THE CAST : Probably my very first problem with this movie - None of the characters I felt invested in, and the second roles shone way more than the 2 protagonists, Maren ( Taylor Russell ) and Lee ( Timothée Chalamet ). They are lifeless, boring, unconvincing. They have about as much chemistry as water and oil do. We're somehow supposed to believe those two love each other to death in such a short time, and while I know young love can be intense, this is not what's accurately represented here. Lee and Maren are together by default , because ' they're the same '. That's all. We don't see them having any real meaningful conversations, we just see them be . Which again, would be fine if they had that spark, but they just do not. THE SFX : The very few gory scenes are very well executed and I honestly wished there would have been more. For a movie which the literal main theme is cannibalism, there is almost none of it on screen (or off, for that matter). THE SOUND : Oh man, that fucking acoustic guitar. Those damn 4 accords we keep hearing all throughout the movie just about drove me crazy. Every time a conversation ended, or an important scene did, we had those zoom outs accompanied by that guitar trying to be melancholic. Of what , exactly ? I couldn't tell you. This movie desperately tries to be mellow, bittersweet and contemplative, but it fails in all regards. It's just slow and vapid. You should have seen the face I made when I recognized Trent Reznor 's voice at one point (in what I learned was the title song). I still cannot believe this literal genius of a composer did this score. If it wasn't for (obviously) hearing his voice; I would have never associated Reznor (nor Atticus Ross) to this movie. THE CINEMATOGRAPHY : This is the only good part of this movie, the way it looks. If you look at the trailers, it is absolutely beautiful, the dialogue sounds heartfelt, the feelings of the characters seem intense, it looks so good. Sadly, when spread accross two excruciating hours and eleven minutes, the cinematography isn't going to be enough. Despite it being gorgeous, I still have some gripes with it; to me, the filming lacked any kind of dynamism - it actually does feel like a 2h music video at times. And believe me, I love contemplative films. This one just wasn't it for me. IN THE END : Bones and All seems like a failed promise. From the moment Maren meets Lee, the movie ironically goes downhill. It wants to be controversial but just doesn't go far enough, then take that back and tries throwing us off with disgusting, shocking  characters, but they're never an actual threat. It all falls short. And every time the protagonists do something reprehensible, they are excused, justified by their ' nature ' and the very quick and basic remorse Maren sometimes shows. Their personal set of morals is discussable too; as the only person we see the couple feeding on together is a gay guy that Lee kills in a cornfield (only after sex, for some reason), but when Maren discovers he was married to a woman with a kid, suddenly, she freaks out. Ok girl. In the end, what bothers me most probably is the parallel this film obviously tries to make, using cannibalism as an analogy. The poster says " You can't run from who you are ", pretty much making them being cannibals their whole identity, making it unquestionnable, while the movie itself fights tooth and nails to make them appear desperately human. Final note : 2/10 . Bones and All had -everything-, and I truly mean everything , on paper, to appeal to me. But I found nothing enjoyable aside from the visuals, and then again, not for 2+ hours. As I often say to myself, " This would have been a great 40min short ".

Träumer Kino der schönsten und seltsamsten Sorte, das vielleicht gar nicht so das großartige Werk mit Metaphern aufgeladen ist, sondern eher eine kleine sympatische Kuriosität. Bones and All würde ist ein wenig bizarr und voller Gegensätze, aber im Kern würde ich sagen, es ist eine Außenseiter-Story, wie man ein Leben lebt mit einem let's call it "Lebensstil", der als problematisch angesehen wird. Dazu gehört sowas wie, dass sobald das Leben unerträglich wird, man Gleichgesinnte findet, die einem Halt geben, das Konzept fatalistischer Liebe und natürlich ganz viele Bilder, die ein Midwest-Roadtrip so gemütlich machen, wie man ihn sich nur vorstellt. Der krasse Gegensatz ist dann natürlich der Part, wo Maren und ihre vielen Bekanntschaften Menschen essen, aber auch das wird weirdly eklig faszinierend eingefangen und wirkt gegen Ende fast schon karthatisch. So ganz konnte ich mir keinen Reim auf diesen Aspekt der Geschichte machen, aber wie gesagt ist der Film sehr laid back und hat mir eher etwas Komfort mit dem Gefühl gegeben, wenn man im Leben einsam ist und sich anders und missverstanden fühlt. In gewisser Weise ist es auch ein Coming of Age Film. Aus Marens Perspektive beginnt ihr Leben erst so richtig, als ihr Vater sie zurücklässt und sie die Welt auf eigene Faust, ohne einen Vormund, entdeckt. Sie lernt noch viele andere Menschen wie sie kennen und irgendwann wird klar, dass im ganzen Land eine Art Community existiert, die ihre Dränge unterschiedlich ausleben, aber alle versteckt vor der allgemeinen Gesellschaft leben. An der Stelle geht der Lebensstil von Maren und Lee auch perfekt mit der im Midwest geprägten Armut einher. Man kann sich nirgends niederlassen, entwickeln, ist generell misstrauisch und kann morden und rauben wie es einem beliebt, weils eh kaum jemand nachverfolgt. Am Ende ist Bones and All für mich weniger Horror oder große Metapher als einfach ein stimmungsvoller Roadtrip über Einsamkeit, das Heranwachsen und das Bedürfnis, irgendwo dazuzugehören. Nicht jede Idee geht für mich komplett auf, aber Luca Guadagnino erschafft daraus so eine eigenartige Wohlfühlmelancholie, dass ich mich in der seltsamen Perspektive von Maren und Lee total verloren habe.

Beautiful film. Luca did such a good job at balancing romance and horror, which are two polar opposites. The feeding scenes of the eaters were disgusting and incredibly gruesome, but watching it still felt warm somehow. Maybe it’s the muted colors and the strings that recurred throughout the film. My God, it was beautiful. I can’t believe I didn’t appreciate it as much before as I do now. Whatever they’re doing, killing and eating people, is morally wrong and just blatantly evil, but I can’t help but root for Maren and Lee. Whatever they had felt so calm and true, and they were really only like that with each other. ‘Di ko magets mga nagsasabing wala silang chemistry, to be honest kasi … kita niyo ba mga halikan scenes nila hahaha? I wanted the film to end when they had normal lives. They looked so happy. But the ending just made everything so much more painful to watch, andddd I’d watch it over and over again. It was so beautiful. What they had was bound to end eventually. Sabi nga nila, “Let’s be them for a while .” It wasn’t meant to last because they were pretending all along. I do wonder if they really had a choice, though. Maren actively decides not to eat people, but she eventually succumbs to it. Maybe cannibalism is intrinsic to them. Maybe they can stop for a while, eat their hands or whatnot in hopes of saving the people they love, but it all surfaces eventually, which is heartbreaking because it gets in the way of so many beautiful things. Or maybe… maybe they had a way out; they just didn’t know how. Siguro dito hindi magiging applicable ‘yong “if he wanted to, he would” hahahah. Ano ‘yun, final act of love niya ay ipinakain sarili niya para maging part siya ni Maren forever? Alam ko namang madali lang para sa kanila, well, for most of them at least, na mag move on sa mga kinakain nila, pero kung ako si Maren, ‘di talaga ako makakausad after niyan. Hay buhay talaga. What a painfully beautiful ending.

From the terrifying first trailer to the scathing reviews, I knew at some point in my life I was going to watch Cats. It was too much of an anomaly, too high-budget a disaster for me to ignore, I didn’t want to watch it, I HAD to see just how bad it was. And fuck me was this an absolutely terrifying fever dream filled with an uncomfortable amount of drugs, sex and music without having any drugs or sex and too much music. I’m genuinely scarred for having seen it all the way through. Let’s start with the plot. There isn’t any. And I’m not just saying that to be funny, this entire film is 90 minutes of introductions, 10 minutes of actual story and the other 10 minutes is weird panting and gyrating. Here I’ll give you a rundown of what happens; we open with our lead Victoria being abandoned by her owners, she’s introduced to the Jellicle Cats with their Jellicle Ball – and sidenote, they never explain what a Jellicle is and why it’s important to be one despite them saying Jellicle about 587 fucking times in the first five minutes – who take her to see the cats hoping to become the Jellicle choice and live a new life in the fucking sky or something. I swear to Christ, the little plot I can recognise as a story makes me think this is about a fucking suicide cult. From there Victoria meets Rebel Wilson’s hairy cooch, Jason Derulo’s CGI bulge, James Corden’s fat arse, a couple thieving twins who I couldn’t tell if they were related or not because of the fuck me eyes they were flashing at each other, Judi Dench’s old face and Ian McKellen making Meow noises before we actually get to the Jellicle Ball in which the contestants are STILL being introduced since the bad guy – Idris Elba and his unnervingly smooth fur body – has been stealing all the contestants with magic – oh by the way there’s fucking MAGIC in this film, they kinda dropped that on you without warning – so anyone who’s still taking part in the Ball we’ve never fucking seen before, making their musical numbers an exercise in futility because I don’t know them and I don’t want to fucking know them. Those two paragraphs cover around 80% of the story, all this film has is cats introducing themselves through song for an hour and a fucking half and then getting lucky if they have anything to say afterwards. It’s not a plot, it’s a fucking 2 hour montage of people we’ve never seen before and it doesn’t stop, new characters are still being introduced with their own numbers with over half the film already done. The only time it actually works is with Mr Mistoffelees who, despite a fairly low amount of screen-time, has been shown to be a cowardly magician and needs confidence to do Big Magic, that works but it comes so late into the game that it couldn’t save the rest of this train wreck. And before anyone dares defend this film, I know it’s based on a musical and I know it’s a different medium, but Hamilton managed to tell an entire historical story with only singing, this is just cats singing about themselves without a story to give them a reason to sing about themselves. The cast is absolutely stacked with big names who are given nothing to work with, and the ones that have something are the weakest actors in the film, I feel kinda bad for Francesca Hayward who plays Victoria because she’s suppose to be our lead, our surrogate into this bizarre, fucked up world of the Jellicle Cats and she’s given nothing, out of all the speaking parts she has probably the fewest amount of lines, every face she makes has this big wondrous smile about EVERYTHING, no matter how benign, and sure she dances well but in a film where everyone is dancing that doesn’t stand out. This is Hayward’s big theatrical break and she’s the most forgettable element in the film, which ironically might save her career. Out of everyone Victoria meets during the many MANY introductions she has to suffer through, not one of them make it worthwhile to sit through their number. Jason Derolo  - who I just hate in general anyway – sings about how Rum Tum Tugger  is a fussy little cunt then screams for milk, Mungojerrie and Rumpleteazer were the thieving twins who looked like they wanted to do a furry version of a Bratty Sis video, and I didn’t know they were twins until writing this review so that just knocks the film even lower for me. There was also a tap dancing train conductor who serves no fucking purpose, Ray WInstone hissing and wondering where the fuck his career has gone and Taylor Swift who even in a film filled with unnecessary sexual energy, gave off too much sexual energy. Seriously man, I got Lola Bunny flashbacks during her number. Worst of the lot was Rebel Wilson and James Corden as Jennyanyfots and Bustopher Jones respectively, I already dislike these two before going into the film and having them both talk the most out of almost any other character was a kick in the fucking dick. Wilson’s introduction was this disturbing piece where she did the most unsexy sexy poses while the camera focussed on her naked hairy body before bringing in singing mice and marching cockroaches with human faces which Jenny proceeds to eat several of when she’s not singing. Corden meanwhile sings for five minutes about being a fat fuck and eating a lot, that’s the entirety of his character, he’s fucking fat, and the fact that both of them are just allowed to skit and makes shitty jokes is simultaneously distracting from the actual plot while adding nothing to the plot either. Both of them were just playing themselves in fur suits and like I said I think both are fucking overdone anyway so I didn’t give a shit about them either way. The only people I see coming out of here unscathed are Ian McKellen and Judi Dench who both have strong enough careers to look past this blip, although Dench’s monologue at the end where she looks at the camera goes on WAY too long about how a cat is not a dog (the fuck?) and every pause makes you think that it’s finally over but no, she keeps fucking going. Jennifer Hudson as Grizabella should also be ok, despite being important to the film she only has three scenes but among those three is her version of the famous ‘Memories’ number which is unironically good, hell I’d say too good for this turd of a film. I’m also hoping that Idris Elba comes out of this unaffected, his villain Macavity is suitably villainous and his motivations generically evil enough – he wants to be the Jellicle Choice because Fuck You I guess – that Elba can work something out with the material but between nobody being able to recognise the most wanted cat in town and his own horrifying nude cat-body, I doubt he’s getting away from this thing clean. Director Tom Hooper has done a few things of note over the last few years, namely his last three films were all Oscar winners and he brought Les Mes to the big screen so I can see why he’s be chosen for this. But holy hell does he fuck this up, this has to go down as one of the biggest fuck-ups of direction of the 21st Century because while Hooper doesn’t do anything technically wrong, nothing he does is done right. Let’s get the big one out of the way; the cats look fucking weird, I knew the cats looked weird, I saw the trailer, I saw the memes, but nothing prepared me for the seeing them in full CGI horror, the first time I saw a Cat-Man clamber down a brick wall, looking like a human being contorting their body into some kind of fucking Cronenberg nightmare with a tail I realised that this was so much worse than I thought it was going to be. It’s the deepest level of the uncanny valley I’ve seen since The Rock in The Mummy Returns and that was 18 fucking years before this, nobody looks human but they don’t look like a cat either, they’re a disgusting hybrid of the two, these vaguely human looking faces pasted onto what looks like skin-tight cat-suits made with actual cat flesh, it NEVER sits right with you. What makes it even more uncomfortable is that there seems to be no rhyme of reason to the clothing, a few cats wear clothing but most of them are nude and some of them even take off their clothes making them nude and I’m left wondering if this is just a nudist colony with lax rules or if everyone is suppose to be naked and we’re just suppose to accept it. I know I shouldn’t be this focussed on naked cat people but I can’t help it, this movie has forces naked cat people into my fucking brain and given me no fucking logic about why they’re naked, hell I haven’t even touched upon the Rebel Wilson scene where she unzips her naked fur-body, as  in literally takes off her skin, to reveal a dance outfit underneath. It’s the tightness as well, I don’t know why they went out of their way to make the cats sexy but it just feels wrong, all the naked cat actors have all their curves pronounced so that every breast, every bulge, every butt covered in fur is on full display but without any form of genitals. Elba gets the worst of it because his fur colour is identical to his skin colour leaving him looking like a fucking Ken Doll with ears but not one person looks good like this. And that’s not even talking about how horny this film is, I heard the stories, I read the reviews that talked about how sexual the film was but it’s not until you’re seeing this cat people twist their bodies together, panting in unison and nuzzle into each other that you have to take a step back and realise that humans doing cat actions is trying way too hard to be sexy whilst not trying to be sexy. The Jellicle Ball is the most horrific example, it’s the hissing, the panting, the Judi Dench hairy leg spread, I honestly couldn’t tell you if the film was trying to be this sexual and went way too far or if it wasn’t trying at all and just came off that way by accident. I haven’t even touched upon the fucking music because I don’t know how to, the visual disaster overpowers the audio so much that I can’t tell if anyone actual sung during this film or not. Ok, over exaggeration, a few songs worked but only a few, the aforementioned Memories hit well and I was fine with the Mr Mistoffelees number but outside of them I really can’t remember any of the songs being any good. The opening introduction to the Jellicle Cats was upbeat I guess, I was too distracted by the CONSTANT use of Jellicle, Jennyanydots was too distracting with the human cockroaches and under-skin dress change for me to even remember what the song was. Tugger and Bustopher were both boring, end of discussion, McKellen’s small number as Gus felt like a lot of build-up for a limp-dick crescendo and Swift’s piece of Macavity trying to big him up almost worked as a villain song if I wasn’t distracted by the complete lack of Idris Elba penis. Before this film the only knowledge I had of Cats was hearing Memories here and there and the rape story from Team America, having now seen this film I know even less about Cats and I don’t want to know anything more about Cats. This is one of the strangest, most confusing, unsettling and fucked up pieces of cinema I’ve ever seen that wasn’t an intentional horror movie, I’ve never seen anything like Cats so 10/10 for uniqueness but just because nobody’s done it before doesn’t mean it’s a good idea and Cats the Movie was not a good idea. There’s no story, all we have is oversexed sexless Cat People introducing themselves for 2 hours before nothing happens and the film ends, nobody looks good, only a couple sound good, the CGI is a mess, the sexiness uncomfortable, the songs forgettable and the whole experience traumatising. I’d say you have to see it just to get the full picture yourself but honestly you’re safer avoiding this. 2/10

I watched this film three times in theatres. It was my sophomore year of high school and one of the first films I saw when the theatres reopened. Snowbanks piled outside of the theatre, making those tall industrial lampposts seem small by comparison. I begged my friends to join me to watch this film—, which I had been raving about. Not because I thought it was technically apt, not by any stretch would I make such an argument now or then. No, because I found it hypnotic. We ascended the crusted snowbanks and into the theatre. The final viewing there was only six people in the theatre. My two friends and I, and three grown men in the very back row. For the first twenty minutes or so they meowed at us, and naturally we meowed back. By the end of the film I was overcome by what I can only describe as a psychedelic euphoria. My friends and I, as well as the men danced in front of the theatre screen together—, meowing along to the music. We never spoke a word to those men, I don’t think we ever clearly saw their faces, only backlit silhouettes only further eroded by the joy of human connection. This is a moment that will flash before my eyes on my death bed. This is the high I will forever chase and nothing will ever compare. This is why I love Cats.

Im slightly biased towards cats. It was the musical that made me fall in love with musical theatre and why have such an appreciation for it. Which may sound strange since it is so hated. In my defence i was young so i was easily impressed. So i don’t hate this film. It’s not amazing either. I think its biggest problem for me is the visuals. The whole cgi human/cats plus the cgi back grounds are severely distracting. I think if the set felt more real and they were in costume like the stage musical it may have looked better. Although cats is difficult since they are cats… I think the stage costumes could have such potential and the movie’s costumes could have been a strong point. Along with the costuming, the music and dancing are strong points for this musical. I wish it allowed more space for the dancing, less close up shots. The dancing cant be fully appreciated since the cgi cat/humans are distracting. I think the better visual would help highlight this, along with hiring strong dancers and ballerinas. The plot of cats is weak. I think the movie could have taken the opportunity to add a conflict to move the plot further. Maybe adding another song or two, along with beautiful ghost. A little more about victoria and how abandoned she is, her need to fit in with these cats she has met. Another point is the script/jokes which are also weak. If the writers/director were wanting to make a cats movie, i think expanding on it rather than a straight up adaptation would make more sense. The musical itself is weak in many areas. So the movie is weak and doesn’t exactly work because what works on stage does not guarantee it works on film. I think they should have made some serious changes. I also feel it lacks context, which leaves it confusing and boring at times. Maybe could have had Judy Dench narrate the film? The ending was of the film was underwhelming and the last song was boring. I enjoyed the film, i haven’t seen it since it came out. I just feel it is wasted potential. Maybe even a pro shot would have made more sense. Theres worse films out there. To be fair there is also better films out there.

My review of Cats (or A Stoner's Journey Into The Heart of Darkness) DISCLAIMER : This review is in no way an endorsement of the movie, please view at your own risk. (Mild Spoilers Ahead) So I finally find did something I had been considering for some time now. I got high and watched Cats and it nearly broke me. To preface, the choice to watch this movie on that very nigjt wasn't exactly random. If you follow me you might know that, immediately before this, I had watched a weird little gem of French cinema called Car Cemetery, a surreal punk rock "musical" mixing grimy, torturous and explicit sexual acts with messianic parable all while taking place in a post-apocalyptic junkyard. In my review of the movie I joked that it was "queerer than Cats." Not having seen Cats before and having an appreciation for strange and queer cinema, naturally I decided to put my money where my mouth is and challenge my assumptions on the matter. From the opening and throughout the first 10-15 minutes of the film I was engaged in an uncontrollable fit of hysterical laughter that seemed unstoppable despite my will to breathe. So early into the film, yet, had I already gone mad? How could this have been made with any intention other than to create a lovecraftian nightmare of fur and surreal landscapes. I believe the terror really set it about the time the Rebel Wilson Cat was concluding her number and began making unmistakeably suggestive petting motions. It was then I began to realized that all of these characters were trapped in an existential race towards death. The performers vying for the coveted "Jellical Choice" for their own reasons wanted to die. They were competing to prove which cat has suffered the most in whichever iteration of their 9 lives this was. Fear then turned to despair and however weird it was staring at Jennifer Hudson's face mapped onto a cartoonish cat body was not enough to distract me from the pain of existence that floated on every vocalization of "Memory." And then, just as it always does, the pain and suffering led to apathy. Maybe I too in some small way wanted to die, to move on from this nightmarish jest. Or maybe my hightened state of consciousness was just wearing off and I was getting bored. By the time the feline personification of Jennifer Hudson started floating off into the sunrise destined for reincarnation, I began foolishly searching for a deeper meaning to the whisical chaos of the film. Do cats experience God like humans are known to do? Does time exist as an infinite line or does it loop-de-loop over and over again until our astral bodies fade from existence. But alas the revelation in the form of Dame Judy Dench(s face on a cats body) staring into the camera and singing about addressing your cat with respect. A message which to me hearkens back to the theme of universal suffering, itself a strangely fitting echo of the words of the Great Buddha and the 4 Noble Truths, simplified to express an even more basic truth. We are all here in this reality together, and as we suffer and fight to mold our existence into something a little less distressing, we should always remember to treat all creatures with the respect they deserve. I shockingly rated this film 3 stars, because despite the unintentionally laughable moments, the uncomfortable character design, and all the many WTF moments, I still found myself in appreciation, if for nothing else, than the sheer insanity that resulted in this film. ...Oh yea, and the fact that it's queer as Fuuuuuck!

É, eu sei o que você está pensando... "como assim???" Apenas me escute Quando o trailer de Cats saiu, eu nao tive interesse nenhum nessa bomba, mas aí um dos meus melhores amigos disse que a gente ia ver no cinema. Eu disse a ele: "-Por que você quer fazer isso??? Esse filme claramente vai ser uma chacota, uma vergonha ridícula" "-Eu sei, você não quer muito conferir esse desastre ao vivo???" E de fato, eu não tive resposta pra essa fala, então, um dia depois do Natal fomos a uma vazia sala de cinema pra assistir um filme que já nasceu morto. E foi umas das experiências mais inesquecíveis de cinema na minha vida. Por ter ido sem nenhuma expectativa de que esse filme pudesse ser bom, eu fui capaz de me divertir bastante sem levar nada a sério. A lógica irrealista (e incoerente) de Cats faz com que literalmente qualquer coisa na cena possa ficar muito engraçada por simplesmente estar ali, é como estar vivenciando um delírio de alta definição. Eu ri absurdamente de várias cenas... mas o que é engraçado mesmo é que eu pude sentir um genuíno charme no meio de toda aquela esquisitice. Eu já reassisti Cats várias vezes e os primeiros 30 minutos realmente me entretém, porque são num ritmo muito dinâmico de música e dança que, se você puder desligar o senso crítico, vai só te carregando nessa gracinha de cenas que não tem absolutamente nenhuma história a não ser gatos cantando. Mais pro meio do filme, realmente começa a ficar enfadonho e cansativo, pois o filme começa a se levar a sério, e quando ele tenta se levar a sério aí é realmente só um desastre mesmo. Tecnicamente, é um filme que de fato merece todo o chapisco. O diretor foi um maníaco que quis fazer caprichos técnicos que dificultaram a vida de todos os profissionais que trabalharam na pós-produção do filme, então esse cara merece mesmo ser avacalhado e ter seu trabalho chamado de o pior filme de todos. E é realmente curioso pensar como nomes tao pesados toparam estar no elenco desse filme. Mas sendo muito sincero, assistir Cats no cinema me trouxe uma epifania de que eu me sentia tão envolvido por aquele filme que não importava de nada que ele fosse um desastre. A sua autenticidade ressoou em mim de uma forma que no final, eu quase me convenci de que era um filme bom. Estou frisando isso para que você entenda que eu não estou defendendo a qualidade de Cats. Estou apenas dizendo que não importa ele ser ruim Às vezes, nós deveríamos só assistir mais filmes ruins e nos entregar à liberdade de não esperar nada do que estamos assistindo. Praticar o exercício de apenas nos entregarmos na experiência de uma obra, e assim percebermos que talvez, um filme ruim também possa te oferecer uma coisa boa. Um filme ruim pode ser engraçado pra caralho. No pior dos casos você ainda vai treinar mais o seu senso crítico. Hoje em dia é tão fácil ser exigente e crítico com tudo, que eu sinto que a coisa mais saudável a se fazer seria realmente, não assistir todo filme do mundo esperando que ele seja bom, mas que seja pelo menos interessante. E isso vai de encontro a uma coisa que eu quero ressaltar: A MAIORIA DAS PESSOAS JULGA ESTE TIPO DE FILME SEM NEM TER SE DADO AO TRABALHO DE VER PRA FALAR MAL. A ESTAS PESSOAS O MEU DESPREZO QUER FALAR MAL???? ASSISTA E TENHA PROPRIEDADE PARA FALAR MAL Pois Cats é um filme horrível mesmo, mas se você se permitir aceitar que ele é horrível, pode talvez conseguir deixar ele te envolver numa experiência lúdica e engraçada, ao fim da qual você vai perceber que ele é um filme ruim de fato, mas nem tanto assim pra criar caso..... Assistam mais filmes ruins, e sejam mais felizes
