Denis Villeneuve en su máximo esplendor. La película es una obra maestra. Realmente magistral. Es de esas películas en las que cuesta encontrar algo que no esté a la altura: el guion, la dirección, la fotografía, los efectos visuales, las actuaciones y, por supuesto, la apoteósica banda sonora de Hans Zimmer. Absolutamente todo funciona. La primera vez que la vi en el cine, en IMAX, salí completamente alucinado. La amé de principio a fin. Pero después de haber leído Dune, la experiencia fue todavía mejor. Amé el libro de Frank Herbert y, precisamente por eso, una de las cosas que más me impresionó de la primera película fue su enorme fidelidad a la obra original. Sin embargo, al leer el libro y volver a Dune: Part Two, entendí que Denis Villeneuve tomó muchas más libertades para llevar la historia hacia una dirección diferente. Y, lejos de molestarme, me pareció maravilloso. Porque eso demuestra que Villeneuve no buscó simplemente trasladar el libro página por página a la pantalla. Entendió su esencia, tomó decisiones propias y construyó su propia visión de Dune. Y eso, para mí, es precisamente lo que hacen los grandes directores. Volver a ver esta película una y otra vez es un verdadero lujo. Cada visionado permite apreciar algo nuevo: la composición de cada plano, los colores, la fotografía, los detalles de los escenarios, la magnitud de Arrakis y el nivel técnico de una producción que visualmente es simplemente impresionante. Y si hablamos de sus grandes virtudes, es imposible no detenerse en la banda sonora de Hans Zimmer. Personalmente, es mi compositor favorito de música para cine y aquí vuelve a entregar un trabajo extraordinario, completamente diferente al de la primera película. Hay momentos en los que basta con cerrar los ojos para sentir el desierto de Arrakis, la inmensidad del planeta y, sobre todo, cómo la tensión va aumentando poco a poco hasta convertir la historia en la promesa de una guerra santa. Las actuaciones también están a un nivel extraordinario. Era algo que podía esperarse después de una primera película con un elenco tan sólido, pero las nuevas incorporaciones elevan todavía más el conjunto. Austin Butler como Feyd-Rautha y Florence Pugh como Irulan son excelentes, pero para mí hay dos que se roban absolutamente la película: Javier Bardem como Stilgar y Timothée Chalamet como Paul Atreides. Chalamet, especialmente, entrega una de las mejores actuaciones de su carrera. Se puede ver en su rostro el tormento, el miedo y el dolor de un hombre que sabe perfectamente hacia dónde lo está llevando el camino que ha elegido, pero que también entiende que cada paso que da puede acercarlo cada vez más al caos que intentaba evitar. Dune: Part Two es una película maravillosa, épica y técnicamente impresionante. Una obra que consiguió conquistar tanto al público como a la crítica y que, en mi opinión, tiene absolutamente merecidos todos los elogios que recibió. Denis Villeneuve tomó una de las obras más importantes de la ciencia ficción, la llevó a la pantalla grande con una visión propia y consiguió convertirla en una experiencia cinematográfica monumental. Una verdadera obra de arte moderna.

this was the film that really helped me out a ton when I first started doing production design- watching interviews with Sam Lisenco (the p.d) introduced me to a new world of film production, and I'm forever thankful for it. finally, after some years, I've come around to see the film that had a huge impact on my aspiring career and deepened my understanding and appreciation of film as a whole. it's a given that what makes this film feel very special is the world and setting of this middle school, the use of intertextuality, and fantastic direction from the character acting, the specific style of cinematography, and the outstanding art direction. This is a very charming coming-of-age story that feels very magical for its modern and internet-age depiction of middle school. I was going into my senior year of high school when this came out, but youth-hood is a timeless experience all the same. In all honesty it would be unfair to compare this to a show like PEN15 because of its lack of social commentary, yes obviously they are both coming of age stories with awkward and anxious preteens, but both pieces of media are accomplishing two different goals. PEN15 has its two female leads, Maya and Anna, who bring a lot of interesting dialogue to be said about race and class in television. Usually I would label a film like this as “white people: the movie” but it would rub me the wrong way doing so as such, so I’ll make a one time exception for this film.

"Growing up can be a little bit scary and weird." — Kayla Day Eighth Grade follows a young person who struggles to express themselves and turns to internet video to build self-confidence. Bo Burnham is recognised for his realistic depiction of the internet, effectively illustrating what motivates people to create content. He presents the internet as a space for self-expression, reflection, and performance, often without an audience, particularly in unwatched vlogs. To ensure authenticity, Burnham cast real eighth graders and addressed mature topics relevant to their age group. The MPAA assigned the film an R rating, which sparked controversy by restricting access for actual eighth graders. In response, A24 organised free, unrated screenings across the United States. This film serves as Generation Z's counterpart to "Thirteen" (2003), though "Thirteen" used lighting to convey its darker themes. In Eighth Grade, students are often absorbed in their phones. Modern mean girls rarely make direct, passive-aggressive remarks, since that would require personal interaction. Instead, they exclude others by ignoring those they consider uncool. While this behaviour is harsh, the film does not portray these popular students as villains. Instead, it shows them coping with their own insecurities. Ultimately, there are no villains in Eighth Grade; the characters are young people trying to understand themselves and their lives. I would love to see another film that is both an interesting social commentary for teens and a generally good film with deep emotional ties that people can relate to.

Oh to be the only girl at the pool party in a one-piece. Kayla, you are everything to me. Putting on makeup before taking a "just woke up like this" selfie. Spending hours trying to engineer the perfect Instagram post like it might somehow engineer a better version of yourself. Every Snapchat story felt like evidence in the case for whether or not you of all people were worth noticing. Eighth Grade understands that before you know who you are, you're already performing as someone else. Every hallway feels like an audience. The boys are impossibly dreamy, the girls impossibly cruel, your parents impossibly embarrassing, and adulthood seems like the cure for it, a glimmer of hope through it all. What a beautiful tragedy it is to be thirteen; how special it is that a movie can almost let us do it all over again.

Wanted to cry for most of this movie. Did cry at several scenes. I love her dad. His monologues are unbelievable. I adore Bo Burnham and his screenwriting. It's incredible how he goes from viscerally cringe dialogue to randomly inserting these subtly beautiful, understated lines. "It's dumb in a way that it's fun to play when it's raining outside" stood out to me for this reason. There's something to be said about how this movie does not use gratuitous violence. I knew what was coming from having shadowed my colleague's film class when this was being covered, but the "bad" scenes still made me nauseous and unsettled. I kept awaiting an escalation, as other popular films have conditioned me to anticipate, and yet the escalation never came. I like that Bo Burnham rejects the spectacle of violence in this respect. Culturally and artistically, we've overly normalized the use of unnecessary violence and brutality in the arts. I'm talking specifically about violence that isn't necessary to plot development. Violence in this respect is used to replace screen-writing that is a) legitimately good and b) trusts the audience's intelligence by instead choosing to depict implied violence. Sure, media literacy is abysmal nowadays, but that's no reason to make art that essentially hinges on the audience's willingness to actively participate in the degradation and oppression of vulnerable, marginalized people (which, for the record, many of the "greats" necessitate we do). Incredibly symptomatic of its time, almost like a time capsule. Missing Bo Burnham's screenwriting a little extra today. Great work.

i don't think anyone will ever understand what this film means to me. i watched it for the first time at 17, when i had already grown out of my preteen awkward phase and somehow considered myself at that point to be a full-fledged adult. but as i watch this film again as a girl in my mid-20s, this stirred something in me i didn’t expect. when i was 17 i saw my younger self in kayla. awkward, anxious, always wanting to be chosen, too shy to talk to the cool kids, and feeling so uncomfortable in my own skin. but at that time of viewing the movie, all i could think was, “thank god that phase is over.” and yes, most of us do not miss that age. but now at 25, i found myself crying with love for this character. that version of ourselves that feels so overdramatic and inexperienced and terrified of growing up, who only a couple of years prior to puberty couldn’t care less if other kids thought she was cool enough. kayla stares at her 6th grade time capsule, addressed on the front “to the coolest girl in the world.” she somehow is depressed and embarrassed that her 11 year old self had that much confidence that her older self would be just that. but it’s that exact kind of confidence that allows us to not only stop judging the awkward versions of ourselves, but to embrace them with our whole hearts. every phase of life is a stepping stone to the next, but every version of ourselves is a part of us. be kind to every age you find yourself in, and cherish it. you grow every day from who you were yesterday, but you don’t forget that awkward girl that got you to where you are today. bo burnham i adore you so much. thank you for this film

Quando comecei o filme, a primeira sensação que tive foi a de estar assistindo a uma versão alternativa de algum filme da Marvel, principalmente uma espécie de Doutor Estranho no Multiverso da Loucura com uma abordagem diferente. Talvez por eu não estar tão acostumado a ver o conceito de multiverso sendo explorado fora do universo dos super-heróis, Tudo em Todo Lugar ao Mesmo Tempo parecia uma ótima oportunidade de enxergar essa ideia por uma perspectiva mais autoral e menos limitada pelas regras de uma franquia. E é curioso porque o conceito de multiverso aqui é muito mais amplo do que simplesmente mostrar versões alternativas dos personagens ou brincar com realidades diferentes. O filme usa essa ideia quase como uma representação das infinitas possibilidades da vida, das escolhas que fazemos e de todos os caminhos que poderiam ter sido seguidos. Essa é uma proposta interessante, e eu gostei da forma como o filme tenta enxergar o multiverso por um lado mais humano e existencial. O problema, para mim, está na forma como essa ideia é apresentada. Em muitos momentos, o filme parece querer ser mais inteligente do que realmente é, como se precisasse constantemente provar sua própria genialidade. A mistura de estilos, o exagero visual e a quantidade absurda de ideias fazem parte da identidade da obra, mas às vezes a sensação é de que o filme força tanto a sua criatividade que acaba perdendo um pouco da naturalidade. Ele quer ser caótico, profundo, engraçado e emocionante ao mesmo tempo, mas em alguns momentos parece mais preocupado em mostrar o quanto consegue ser diferente do que realmente desenvolver tudo aquilo que propõe. Eu gostei mais do ato final justamente porque é o momento em que o filme finalmente parece entender a própria força. Depois de passar boa parte da duração mergulhado em um caos constante, entre cortes frenéticos, exageros visuais e uma tentativa quase desesperada de ser irreverente, ele finalmente desacelera e permite que seus personagens existam de verdade. É quando Tudo em Todo Lugar ao Mesmo Tempo deixa de tentar provar o tempo todo o quanto é criativo e começa a explorar aquilo que realmente tinha de mais interessante: as relações humanas por trás de todo aquele espetáculo. Antes disso, porém, eu tive muita dificuldade de me conectar com a proposta. Não é pelo fato de o filme ser absurdo ou querer ser engraçado, porque essa é claramente a identidade dele, mas pela forma como ele constantemente interrompe os próprios momentos de profundidade. Sempre que surge uma oportunidade de desenvolver melhor suas ideias sobre arrependimentos, escolhas e a sensação de insignificância diante de infinitas possibilidades, o filme parece escolher quebrar a atmosfera com uma piada que muitas vezes não funciona e acaba tirando todo o peso daquilo que estava sendo construído. E isso acaba prejudicando justamente a profundidade que ele tenta alcançar. Algumas cenas são tão forçadas e constrangedoras que, ao invés de aproximarem o espectador dos personagens, criam uma distância. O filme quer ser caótico, divertido e emocionante, mas em muitos momentos o caos domina tanto que a parte humana fica escondida. Só quando ele finalmente abandona um pouco essa necessidade de transformar tudo em uma grande piada é que a mensagem começa a encontrar espaço para respirar. Eu realmente acredito que a campanha desse filme no Oscar foi um delírio coletivo. Sinceramente, não consigo enxergar uma obra digna de sete estatuetas aqui. Para mim, o único prêmio realmente justificável é o de Melhor Montagem. Todo o restante parece premiar mais a ideia do filme do que a sua execução. É uma obra que força a própria genialidade, insiste em uma profundidade que raramente alcança e, justamente quando parece prestes a dizer algo verdadeiramente significativo, escolhe sabotar o momento com um humor que, para mim, soa artificial e deslocado. E no fim, eu continuo com a sensação de que assistir a Tudo em Todo Lugar ao Mesmo Tempo não foi uma experiência tão distante de assistir a um filme da fase 4 da Marvel. Talvez exista mais criatividade na forma, uma identidade visual mais autoral e uma ambição maior nas ideias, mas a essência ainda me parece muito semelhante. O multiverso continua sendo tratado como um grande espetáculo, onde tudo precisa ser maior, mais caótico e mais excêntrico do que o anterior. Se a Academia decidiu premiar justamente esse tipo de proposta com o maior prêmio da noite, então talvez fosse mais coerente ter reconhecido um dos próprios filmes da Marvel, que, gostando ou não, sempre assumiram esse espetáculo sem a necessidade de revesti-lo com uma profundidade que, para mim, aqui nunca se concretiza.

Tudo em Todo o Lugar ao Mesmo Tempo (2022), de Daniel Kwan e Daniel Scheinert, é um filme cuja inventividade visual é inegável. A direção de arte, o uso das cores e a composição dos quadros sustentam um espetáculo imagético que raramente deixa a tela perder energia. O problema é que, conforme a narrativa avança e os conflitos centrais começam a aparecer, essa exuberância formal passa a competir com o próprio drama. Em vários momentos, o filme me lembrou um episódio estendido de Rick and Morty, insistindo o tempo inteiro em provar o quanto é "maluco" e "criativo", mas girando em torno da mesma dinâmica até ela perder o impacto. O excesso vira um fim em si mesmo, quase um exercício de estilo, e a montagem acelerada acaba produzindo uma sensação de clipe permanente. As discussões sobre família, identidade e aceitação existem, mas parecem sempre mediadas pelo humor e pelo absurdo, como se o filme não confiasse que essas ideias conseguiriam se sustentar sem um novo estímulo a cada poucos segundos. Isso enfraquece a construção psicológica dos personagens: muitas mudanças simplesmente acontecem, sem que a mise-en-scène ou o roteiro construam um percurso emocional convincente até elas. Soma-se a isso um niilismo já bastante desgastado, aquele discurso de que "nada importa porque o universo é infinito", tratado como se ainda fosse uma grande revelação filosófica. No fim, fiquei com a impressão de um filme que confunde complexidade estrutural com profundidade dramática. Multiplicar universos, referências e estímulos não torna uma narrativa automaticamente mais complexa; às vezes só faz mais barulho do que significado.

Went in with zero expectations. Didn't need logic, didn't need deep character work — just wanted something genuinely fun and entertaining. And honestly, I just ended up bored. The whole “genre-blending” thing isn't as wild as people say. Sure, it jumps between worlds and tosses in sci-fi, action, and some emotional moments, but none of it ever actually blends into something fresh or mind-blowing. It's just a movie that changes costumes without ever becoming genuinely entertaining. The multiverse stuff, which is supposed to be the big selling point, got repetitive fast. They create a couple of cool, weird worlds early on, but then keep revisiting the same handful over and over. “Everything Everywhere All at Once” quickly shrinks into “a few things, a few places”. That killed the sense of endless possibility and just made it feel small and monotonous. Also, people praise the relentless pace, but I honestly didn't feel it. The editing is busy, not fast — there's a difference. Especially the last hour dragged like crazy. So many slow-motion moments that didn't earn their weight, stretching out scenes that already felt emotionally repetitive. And the humor? The problem isn't that the jokes are random or dumb — it's that the movie never commits to real chaos. It gives you a couple of weird ideas, then just keeps circling back to them until they're completely worn out. A truly random, limitless multiverse should be throwing something new at you constantly, but instead the jokes become predictable, cliché, and as limited as the worlds themselves. That's really the core issue here: the movie runs out of ideas and then just stretches everything thin, repeating itself because it doesn't know what else to do. If you're going to be this narratively limited, you'd better have deep characters, sharp logic, or some real emotional weight to fall back on — and it has none of that. The emotional beats are so forced, practically holding up cue cards that say “care now” and “cry here”. Given how wild and limitless the premise is, the ending lands as preachy, cliché, and a total drag — exactly the kind of safe landing a film like this should have avoided. Honestly, it's not that different from plenty of other weak films that start with a decent premise and then fumble it. The only difference is this one got a sky-high rating and a pile of Oscars.

بصراحة، هذا من أكثر الأفلام التي لم أفهم سبب كل هذا التقدير الذي حصل عليه. لا أنكر أن فيه مجهودًا إخراجيًا واضحًا، وأن الإخراج مليء بالأفكار البصرية المبتكرة، كما أن التمثيل كان جيدًا، خصوصًا من الأبطال الرئيسيين. لكن بالنسبة لي، هذه الجوانب لم تكن كافية لتجعل الفيلم تجربة عظيمة. المشكلة الأساسية عندي كانت في الفكرة نفسها. شعرت أنها بسيطة جدًا، بل وتذكرني بأفكار كانت موجودة في بعض الأعمال الكرتونية القديمة، مع إضافة عناصر حديثة لم تعجبني إطلاقًا. كذلك احتوى الفيلم على بعض الموضوعات والعلاقات التي لم أجد أنها أضافت قيمة للعمل، بل جعلتني أنفر منه أكثر. في النهاية، هذا مجرد رأيي الشخصي، لكن احترامًا لحبي للسينما وتقديري للأفلام التي تترك أثرًا حقيقيًا، أقول إن هذا الفيلم لم ينجح معي إطلاقًا، وأراه فيلمًا سيئًا رغم كل الإشادة التي حصل عليها. ⸻ Honestly, this is one of the films whose acclaim I simply don’t understand. I won’t deny that the direction is ambitious and visually inventive, and the performances are solid, especially from the lead cast. However, none of that was enough to make it a great experience for me. My biggest issue was the core concept itself. It felt surprisingly simplistic, reminding me of ideas that had already been explored in older animated works, only with modern additions that I personally didn’t enjoy. I also found some of the themes and relationships in the film unnecessary and distracting rather than meaningful. In the end, this is only my personal opinion, but out of respect for my love of cinema and the films that truly leave a lasting impact, I have to say that this one simply didn’t work for me. Despite all the praise it received, I consider it a poor film.

By balancing destructive nihilism with joyful absurdism, the film captures how small human connections can heal the deep wounds of generational trauma. This movie perfectly showcases the complexities of Asian cultural dynamics, as parental love is often masked as strict criticism and heavy expectations to protect the family’s future. This creates a painful cycle of conditional love, leaving a feeling unseen and burdened by the pressure to be perfect. Seeing this with my Asian mother was the cherry on top of this already deeply resonating experience.

Außerdem war die Story mit den Steinen auch richtig gut und die Kampfszene wo sie mit den beiden Typen kämpft, die was im Arsch stecken haben ist absolute Cinema. Das Worldbuilding ist auch richtig interessant und die Menge an verschiedenen Kostümen und Designs ist verrückt. Ich liebe dass sich dieser Film absolut nicht ernst nimmt und dann an den wichtigen Stellen es doch wieder macht. Ich kann diesen Film wirklich nur empfehlen, er ist wunderschön und sehr lustig.

Admit it—most people remember Friday the 13th (2009) for all the wrong reasons like the overwhelming amount of nudities. This is just another typical slasher film: an unstoppable killer hunting down a group of unintelligent teenagers, with some protected by plot armor and others serving as disposable victims. One thing that genuinely annoyed me was the death of one of the nicest characters, who deserved a much better fate.

Thus my Crystal Lake journey comes to an end (at least until October). I don't know if I just have Stockholm syndrome or if it was just anti-remake culture that was prevalent when I first watched this, but this movie isn't really that bad. It's still pretty mediocre, it's definitely not an Evil Dead (2013) situation, but in comparison to the following year's Nightmare On Elm Street reinvention, it might as well as be a masterpiece. This film has a real nasty edge with some properly gnarly gore, which does give it its own identity. It kinda surprises me that this is the only outing, which utilises a bear trap, especially because Part 2 sets up that Crystal Lake is bear country, however it does   lead to delightfully horrific results. I'm sure a lot of this is due to the filmmakers wanting to compete with the "torture porn" craze of the time, yet they do manage to hold their own well enough. The unfortunate over side to the grossness coin, it's how much aggressively juvenile misogyny is on display, leering at its female characters in a way only a Micheal Bay produced flick can. Similarly, the American Pie style sex comedy (outside of a few jokes) feels very tired and just unnecessarily unpleasant. The characters are a bit of a nothing burger, although not in a way significantly different than most entries and there's a few good performances scattered in. At first glance, the idea of combining story elements from the first four installments into one narrative sounds like a recipe for disaster, yet those movies are either a bit repetitive or rather simple, that it actually kind of works. The script wasn't gonna awards, the dialogue is far too clunky and there are dumb character decisions and contrivances galore, but some thought clearly went into it. Overall, if you stayed away from this because it's a 2000s horror remake, first of all... Fair. Nonetheless, you can do much much worse.

So we’ve got Dean Forester from Gilmore Girls, Kyle Bradway from Party Down, and Jonah Simms from Superstore. Essentially it’s Avengers Endgame for streaming binges. Watching this I can understand why young people say millennials are the worst generation. Be that as it may, I kind of enjoyed this. More so, admittedly, than most of the movies in this franchise.

You know what, I really love how aggressive Jason is here. Gone is the stiff stalker from the 80s, and instead, we get a rabid animal. He moves quickly and doesn’t hesitate to brutalize. I did feel it was somewhat disappointing, however, that despite how aggressive he is, the kills aren’t overly memorable. Rewatching this after my recent marathon was helpful just in helping me notice how they tried to piece together the various eras and foundational lore of the original films into one story. That progression mostly works. Despite it being a noticeably better-made film when compared to many of its predecessors, it still feels like a very mediocre slasher. While some of the older films were boring cash grabs, others had fun. Saw this in the theater when I picked up the His Name Was Jason DVD, which came with a free movie ticket for the remake. I wonder if sales of that disc counted towards the box office numbers? I only wonder because this thing had a historic second weekend drop-off that basically killed the franchise in the mainstream until the video game came out. I remember seeing trailers for Miss March and the remake of Last House on the Left before the movie started. Even at the time, Miss March felt like it was trying to ride some kind of American Pie wave that had long ago hit the shore and settled back into the seas - no wonder Zach Cregger pretended it didn’t exist when doing the Barbarian press tour. Last House ’s trailer featured a soft girly version of Sweet Child O’ Mine which admittedly felt unique in 2009 compared to the usual Let the Bodies Hit the Floor style nonsense that accompanied horror ads back then. Fast forward to 2026, and the soft-remix trope is one of the top items on my trailer shitlist. You may have noticed I’m not really talking about the movie much, that’s because like all the Platinum Dunes franchise cash-ins of this era, there’s not much to really say. It’s an early 2000’s reboot with that pukey CW Network sheen all over it. To its credit, it was nice to go back to the lake after several entries of goofy nonsense. Trent is one of the all-time douche characters of the entire franchise and Julianna Guill provides some of the best nudity. The kills really should’ve saved this, but aside from the wakeboarding scene, I always struggle to remember any of them even after repeat viewings. If Friday ‘09 (and my accompanying memories at the time of release) is notable for anything, it’s that it was one of the last gasps of the early millennium, and the transition away from things like Drowning Pool, physical media promotions, and raunchy comedies. Watching this feels like a eulogy for the aughts, but as we approach the premiere of a new Crystal Lake series, we know all too well that milking every drop out of a franchise is a timeless endeavor.

So here's the thing, most Friday the 13th films are average. As a series, it doesn't have incredible lows like The Curse of Muchael Myeys or Freddy's Dead, nor the spectacular rebounds like H20 or New Nightmare. It is a series that has remained consistently okay. And that's more or less what this is, another okay entry in the Friday the 13th series. It has all the sex and violence that you expect—actually, a bit more sex than you'd expect for 2009—but doesn't really do much to change up the formula. Ironically, not changing the formula is probably this movie's biggest strength. It's the 12th Friday the 13th movie, and it feels like a Friday the 13th movie. There are some changes that work, some that don't, but overall just an average slasher with a handful of memorable scenes makes for a fairly enjoyable experience if that's your thing. Which weirdly makes it possibly the best of the major horror franchise reboots. Friday the 13th never had the subtext of The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, the quiet suspense of Halloween, or the playful creativity of Evil Dead or A Nightmare on Elm Street. To put it bluntly, there just wasn't really much to fuck up.

I don't think this quite reaches the heights of the best sequels, but it's undeniably a reboot that fundamentally understands the task at hand, and arguably the superior of both Marcus Nispel's 00's horror remakes. Essentially a smooshed-together rendition of the first four original films into a new narrative remix of sorts, after a bit of a ropey opening it skips straight to the good stuff, barrels through the mythology, and gives us Derek Mears' Jason absolutely ruling as a considerably more driven and vicious take on the Hockey Masked killer. I don't really buy the criticisms that it's "too horny", since that promiscuity and lure is kind of part and parcel with the series and its own bizarre detours. The final stretch loses some of the momentum that makes the opening hour such a blast, but the pacing overall is quite relentless, the kills are inventive and nasty, and it's packed with enough of why this series became an institution in the first place. It's a shame it never really spawned anything more, and I look forward to the day we finally get another one of these. Maybe Damien Leone would be a good shout?

KILLER CUT This movie is supposed to suck, but how hard can it be to remake FRIDAY THE 13TH? All you need is Jason slaughtering horny teenagers at Camp Crystal Lake. Should be an easy 8/10. Let’s find out… 🔪🔪🔪 The problem with this movie right away, is that teenagers and young people are portrayed so unnaturally these days. Back in the day, they felt more like real people. Awkward, weird, messy. A lot of it is you would have amateur or non-actors doing some level of improvisation. There is an attempt here to replicate the random weirdness of 80s horror, but it feels manufactured. The cinematography is very bad. The original was creepier because it was mostly natural looking. This remake looks so processed and edited, despite mostly taking place outdoors! It doesn’t look anything like real life. FT13th doesn’t need any of that shit. It’s a guy in a mask in the woods. I don’t want it to look polished into oblivion. By the way, how old are these people? I assumed they were young, but they all look at least 30. I guess it doesn’t matter, though, because they pull the old switcheroo and we get a whole new cast of characters. They also look pretty old. Trent is at least 47. This new group is slightly better, and I’m glad we’re not stuck with the first one. Something that should be commended is that they didn’t change Jason’s look. He looks like he could be from one of the original sequels. “Have you seen a guy carrying a dead body?” There is sufficient violence, I guess, but not any cool practicals. There is some choice nudity, though, which is cool. Julianna Guill is amazing! But yeah, the kills generally weren’t practical or creative. If you’re going to remake a classic slasher, you better have some cool kills in mind. Some of the suspense was successful, and I would probably be more lenient if it was an original property. It’s not terrible, it just doesn’t have enough personality. The end was acceptable. New Line DVD 📀

O Jason do Derek Mears é praticamente o Anton Chigurh dos slashers: paciente, eficiente e inevitável. Enquanto o elenco parece ter saído de um catálogo de comerciais da Abercrombie dos anos 2000, ele faz de Crystal Lake um roguelike: entrou na floresta, morreu, tenta de novo. É engraçado ver como esse filme foi tratado como heresia em 2009 e hoje parece um dos remakes de terror mais honestos da época. Depois de uma década de "terror elevado", às vezes tudo o que eu quero é um sujeito de 2 metros distribuindo machadadas sem precisar representar um trauma intergeracional. Cinema? Talvez não. Entretenimento? Com certeza. E, convenhamos, se você assiste Sexta-Feira 13 esperando a complexidade de Persona, o problema nunca foi o filme.

Friday the 13th (2009) was my first experience with the franchise, and honestly, I had a great time with it. It doesn’t try to reinvent the slasher genre, but it knows exactly what it wants to be, and it delivers an entertaining ride from start to finish. Clay was easily my favorite character. Unlike many slasher protagonists, he isn’t just trying to survive—he’s determined to find his missing sister, and I loved how he never gave up on her. I also appreciated how protective he was of Jenna, which made him someone I genuinely rooted for. Trent was easily my least favorite character. His arrogance and attitude made him impossible to like, so his fate felt well deserved. I also liked that Jason wasn’t portrayed as a completely mindless killer. He follows a distorted logic shaped by his obsession with his mother. Whitney survives because she reminds him of her, which helps explain his actions—but it never excuses them. Understanding a villain’s motives is very different from justifying their crimes. The film doesn’t introduce anything particularly new to the slasher formula, but I honestly didn’t mind. I enjoyed it for what it was, and as my first Friday the 13th film, it definitely made me interested in the franchise. Sometimes a classic formula is all you need when it’s executed with confidence.

I wish I could like Hereditary more. It attempts to tap into a fear not engaged with enough: that is, hereditable disease/mental illness. Formerly, such diseases were incorporated into horror in a mystical or religious way, birth defects being a prime example. Such defects were alternatively viewed as divine or a curse, either being an elevation from normal existence. Now (by that I mean at least since the modern synthesis), with the scientific comphrension of herediability, a new sort of horror has arose. The horror of potentially damning your offspring to a life of suffering, though by no personal fault of your own. In this film, some scenes capture this anxity brilliantly, both from the mom and her son's perspective. Unfortunately, these scenes are invariably undermined by less-than-great acting or by being retroactively neutured (e.g. made into a dream). Even if the individual scene was allowed to breath (rarely), the overarching themes (doll-house, A24 etc), which weren't pulled together well, hampered the cinematography. I did like that the family (namely the father) was supportive, the "curse" of disease can strike anyone. The ending was also provocative (especially when read through the lens of mental illness). Also, maybe its just me (or that I had this movie partially spoiled), but it really wasn't that scary! Probably because it felt so pastiche?

A symphony of gimmicks and muddied waters. I hate to be that person again…. but I genuinely didn’t enjoy this at all. For me, possession/satanic cults and rituals as a trope usually lead to something, to some greater overarching plot. And although not everything needs to have a deeply moving message, this movie unfortunately feels like it lost its own in the process. A lot of the more memorable and twisted scenes only work and have the impact they do because they leverage that early gravitas of the potential exploration of grief, lose of youth/bodily autonomy, familial cycles and traumas, etc. But this film never truly makes that turn around back to the point it initially latched onto and conveniently lets go for the sake of shock factor. I’ll totally be the person to give the actors their flowers, and some of the scenes would not have functioned as such great pieces of storytelling if it was not for the camerawork. But aesthetics and talents can only take you so far. I think this has consistently been my gripe with Ari Aster is he has such great ideas and his attention to detail is insane, but are his grandiose projects fleshed out to begin with? Honestly no. He relies on the conversation and pushing the limits of what horror can be, which I do frankly respect him for; but again this, like a lot of his other work let me go as easily as it grabbed me. And genuinely I’m left with 0 takeaway from this… maybe I’m the problem

Este filme representa, a meu ver, tudo aquilo que há de mais problemático no cinema nacional contemporâneo. É um insulto à tradição artística construída por cineastas que buscaram desenvolver uma linguagem verdadeiramente brasileira para a sétima arte. Saímos da ambição estética e intelectual de Glauber Rocha, responsável por obras fundamentais como Terra em Transe e Deus e o Diabo na Terra do Sol, passamos por realizadores como Nelson Pereira dos Santos e José Mojica Marins, que ajudaram a consolidar uma identidade própria para o cinema brasileiro, para chegarmos a produções como esta, inteiramente subordinadas à lógica do melodrama televisivo e da padronização estética importada do audiovisual norte-americano. O filme permanece preso ao nível mais superficial de apreensão estética. Qualquer sensação de profundidade surge menos de sua construção narrativa do que de expedientes psicológicos cuidadosamente calculados para provocar respostas afetivas automáticas. Tudo parece subordinado à lógica mercadológica: a identidade nacional, a riqueza cultural brasileira e a complexidade dramática são sacrificadas em favor da acessibilidade imediata e da rentabilidade, é o exemplo máximo do Brasil descartando seu cinema como arte para transforma-lo em mero produto e propagando fazendo uma representação porca de sua própria realidade, com um diretor de fotografia sem criatividade e atores que acham que estão em uma novela da globo.

J’avais détesté Central do Brasil de Walter Salles, je trouve Je suis toujours là mauvais également pour des raisons similaires. Le film a la prétention de traiter un sujet « dur » mais il passe la pommade au spectateur pendant 2 heures. La folie et la douleur auxquelles les personnages devraient être sujets sont complètement reniées, tout est fait pour paraître plus doux (le gardien de prison qui est gentil mdrrr j’étais à deux doigts de couper le film). Ensuite, je n’avais jamais vu une famille aussi fonctionnelle, je pense que ça n’existe pas, c’est un fantasme, je n’y crois pas (surtout que les relations ne se fissurent jamais malgré les épreuves). En plus, le personnage principal, celui de la mère, n’existe apparemment qu’à travers son mari et ses enfants, elle n’a pas de personnalité, on ne ressent jamais la douleur et le vide qui pourraient la dévorer. Comme si ce n’était pas déjà assez insupportable, le spectateur est pris par la main constamment (ex : le coup du médicament contre le diabète). Enfin, encore un réalisateur qui filme un animal comme une poupée. Si c’était pour traiter le chien comme un doudou et ne pas en faire un personnage, ce n’était pas la peine (d’ailleurs, quand il meurt on ne sent aucune émotion puisqu’il n’a jamais existé dans le film). Les animaux sont souvent hyper mal utilisés dans les films, dommage. Je ne parle pas de la musique dégoulinante de bons sentiments qu’on se tape régulièrement. Bref, c’est typiquement le genre de films « sUr La rÉsiLieNce » qui donnent la nausée.

بنظر لحظه‌ی وداع تلخ خانواده با خانه‌ی گرم و محبوب‌شان، نقطه‌ی پایان قصه‌ی این خانواده‌ی دوست‌داشتنی در برزیلِ استبدادزده‌ی دهه هفتاد است و یک‌سوم پایانی و پرداختن به دو مقطع زمانی دیگر، کش دادن بیهوده زمان فیلم و تنزل اثر به گزارشی بی‌خاصیت از آینده‌ی این خانواده در جامعه‌ی جدید برزیل است که صرفا ادای دینی‌ غیرسینمایی/غیردراماتیک است به داستان واقعی مورد اقتباس اثر. ارزش فیلم در لحظه‌هایی‌ست که استبداد روح افراد و روحیه‌ی جمعی‌شان را ذره‌ذره به نابودی می‌کشاند (صحنه‌هایی چون انتقال مادر و دختر به بازداشتگاه با کیسه‌هایی روی صورت و یا بعدتر یک لحظه رد شدن مادر نگران از کنار دختر و شناختنش حتی با چشمان بسته). ایکاش پیوند‌های صمیمی و مؤثر پدر با تک‌تک اعضای خانواده و حتی دوستان خانوادگی در ثلث اول فیلم، در نیمه دوم و در خلأ هولناک پیش‌آمده از غیبت مرموزش، دست‌کم در ارتباط با فرزندانش، استمرار بهتری می‌داشت و جای خالی‌اش به اندازه کافی در روابط دیگران حس می‌شد بجای آنکه به مفروضات ظاهرا بدیهیِ عواقبِ یک حکومت مستبد، بسنده میکرد؛ این آثار دهشتناک و بشدت عمیق و پنهانی، در همان لحظات ظاهرا ساده‌ای ساخته میشود که حس میشود دیگر چیزی شبیه قبل نیست؛ زخم واقعی استبداد نه صرفا در بازجویی‌ها و شکنجه‌گاه‌ها که در همین لحظه‌های کوچک و خاموش زندگی روزمره خانه می‌کند؛ مثلا در نگاه دزدکی دختر به مادری که تازه از بازداشتگاه برگشته و در حمام مشغول شستشوی خود با چشمانی اشکبار است یا نگاه دخترک کوچکتر به خانه خالی‌شده‌شان که حرفهای ناگفته زیادی را با خود به همراه دارد.

Apesar de ter muitos méritos, como a atuação poderosa de Fernanda Torres, a bela cinematografia que acompanha todo o filme, a dor de ver uma família destruída por um fato que durou 21 anos no Brasil e a demonstração de como era a perseguição a dissidentes e críticos àquele regime imposto, I'm Still Here erra ao tentar ser um filme e, ao mesmo tempo, uma novela das 9:00 horas produzida pela TV Globo. Isso deve-se principalmente à forma pela qual Walter dirige, monta, cria e coloca os diálogos, constrói a trama e aplica filtros de cores ao seu filme, que remontam diretamente aos modelos e convenções novelísticas moldados por décadas pelas principais emissoras nacionais e internacionais, como as falas explícitas sem a construção do silêncio, as explosões de emoção dos personagens -- o que os faz parecerem um pouco irreais -- e o uso excessivo de meios dramáticos fáceis demais. Uma cena que exemplifica isso é o momento em que as crianças vão ao escritório do pai para mostrar o novo cachorro, pois embora seja uma cena de felicidade das crianças e, consequentemente, de seu pai com o novo cachorro, ela se assemelha muito à construção de cena de dramaturgia, graças aos diálogos, à reação do pai e do colega e à cor pastel que reforçam essa sensação durante todo o longa. A principal explicação desse estranhamento que atravessa a obra tem raízes na forma como o Brasil constrói e construiu suas artes. Desde a popularização do cinema nacional no meio internacional, muitas produtoras e distribuidoras têm escolhido o que é mais fácil e melhor para elas no sentido econômico e cultural: a contratação de atores de novelas para filmes, já que são rostos conhecidos pelo público e têm uma bagagem de atuação muito maior que um ator que está dando seus primeiros passos. Por isso, mesmo nascendo puramente como um longa-metragem, sua raiz pivotal está presa e ligada às novelas, e I'm Still Here sofre com essa dicotomia. Portanto, um dos maiores problemas do cinema nacional é o fato de sempre conversar e ter em seu âmago as regras e padrões da teledramaturgia, não obstante seja uma obra feita para o cinema. Por esse motivo, I'm Still Here , ainda que trate de um assunto pesado e espinhoso que permeia a sociedade brasileira, sofre com crise de identidade, não sabendo se é um drama televisivo ou um longa-metragem -- embora tenha muitos méritos que poderiam atingir seu auge caso se desprendessem das convenções de um meio do qual não faz parte.

In my opinion, this was a questionable choice to be the first Brazilian film to win an Oscar, considering how many stronger and way better films came before it. Like for example the movie "Central Station" by Walter Salles himself who even competed for the same category at the Oscars back in 1999. The performances, dialogues, and script leave a lot to be desired. There’s a lack of depth and good technique that makes it hard to fully connect with the story or its characters. For me, as a Brazilian who has seen so many outstanding films from our cinema, it felt like I was watching one of those generic Netflix movies. It’s not a terrible film, but it doesn’t feel nearly as impactful or deserving of that level of recognition.

Esse filme, nas suas escolha da cena em que em meio aos gritos, o policial diz pra Eunice que “ele não concorda”, ou a cena em que ela tá falando na faculdade que “agora as terras indígenas são demarcadas”, ficarem fazendo questão de falar que o Rubens Paiva não era um guerrilheiro, ou na cena final com ela já idosa observando com todo o rosto cheio afundado em saudade e melancolia a foto de seu esposo que nunca mais voltou (aliás uma das cenas, pra mim, mais impactantes), sendo assistida e cuidada minuciosamente por sua família branca, heterossexual, de classe média em um apartamento no rio/sp, todo mundo de branco indo tirar uma foto, todo mundo sorrindo menos Eunice…De fato há uma mensagem da falta que jamais será preenchida, de buracos que a ditadura realmente deixou, mas tudo me passa a mensagem que o Brasil realmente passou por uma redemocratização, de que além de o problema não ser a polícia enquanto instituição, e sim policiais especificos, que muitos só tinham que seguir ordens mas até “não concordavam com isso”, mas além disso, que agora é totalmente diferente do período da ditadura, que vivemos uma democracia. Acho inevitável deixar de comparar ele com outro filme recente sobre ditadura, é que também tem como escolha a cena final representar “os dias de hoje”, o Agente Secreto, que pra mim apresenta uma visão política, e portanto estética tbm, totalmente diferente da ditadura, comparando as cenas finais por exemplo, em vez de uma família que vive agora relativamente bem e feliz na “democracia brasileira”, temos um filho, agora adulto, sozinho em mais um prédio cinza gelado, que quase tudo de memória que tem do pai, são as fitas recém conquistadas, gravadas na época de sua perseguição por tentar resistir ao domínio empresarial, principalmente dos Estados Unidos sobre a produção de conhecimento, nas faculdades do Brasil durante a ditadura. Acho que o Agente secreto traz a tona a discussão de que não ouve ruptura e muito menos reparação com esse nosso passado tão recente, muito pelo contrário, perspectiva quase oposta ao filme do burguês dono da globo Walter Salles, onde temos a questão da violência policial apresentada quase como uma questão de cpf, não da instituição enquanto uma herança colonial e racista, e mesmo com esse buraco que fica no peito das pessoas que não voltam mais…a vida continua, e continua feliz, sorridente, muito melhor do que antes, enquadrada em uma foto de família feliz…uma perspectiva que nos coloca muito mais numa relembrança passiva, do que num incômodo ativo, uma pulga atrás da orelha sobre como o presente ainda é carregado de passado, de que não essa ruptura com quem nos domina, explora e mata. Enfim, acho ainda estou aqui o pior filme do mundo e muito menos um filme “feio”, ou que não tenha elementos importantes da nossa memória, mas acho que mostra tanto a ditadura quanto os dias de hoje numa perspectiva burguesa e pouco interessada na discussão da memória da classe trabalhadora da ditadura, muito menos na politização da mesma pra enfrentar os impactos desse período obscuro da nossa história no presente. (Também achei bem curiosa essa escolha de falar das terras indígenas hoje serem demarcadas como se fosse algo que hoje é tranquilo, sendo que no gov lula estão tento diversos embates, um seguido do outro, dos povos indígenas lutarem pra defender seu território sendo atacado por garimpeiro ilegal que mesmo assim entra ou lutarem arduamente um mês contra a iniciativa do gov lula de PRIVATIZAR um rio…)

Talvez «Ainda estou aqui» seja uma experiência que ressoe com mais força no público brasileiro. É sempre um desafio equilibrar o drama político sem cair no lugar-comum, especialmente para quem já consumiu o gênero antes. Embora seja um filme educativo e necessário, a obra se prende a uma narrativa previsível e a um ritmo que beira o letárgico. Apesar de composições visuais impactantes, o filme parece não querer arriscar, operando sob uma constante sensação de segurança estilística. Falta-lhe, talvez, um aprofundamento nas nuances ideológicas que cercam a trama; o conteúdo é sombrio, mas a abordagem carece de audácia. O brilho surge, porém, no desfecho. A cena final onde a mulher, que sofre de Alzheimer, encontra um fragmento de resposta é de uma melancolia cortante. É o retrato de uma reparação que chega tarde demais, transformando o encerramento em um momento genuinamente memorável. Disculpem brasileires, não gostei tanto.

Um filme fraco e claramente partidário, com um foco evidente em se posicionar contra a Ditadura Militar. A obra tenta prender o espectador de forma artificial, com cenas forçadas e atuações um pouco exageradas sem muitas "ações evidentes" numa tentativa pouco convincente de fazer o público sentir o que as pessoas daquela época viviam. Mesmo assim, o resultado é ruim. O filme se apoia quase exclusivamente na atuação e, ainda assim, não consegue entregar algo consistente ou impactante. Ou talvez eu não seja “culto” o suficiente para fingir que gostei de algo tão fraco e que não consegue transmitir nem mesmo a única proposta que se impõe. No fim, muitas pessoas se cegam por vieses políticos, independentemente de qual lado seja. E, por isso, relevam a decepção que o filme foi, tratando pontos fracos de roteiro, direção e construção emocional como se fossem virtudes

He’s a competent director but no matter how “sad” Walter Salles’ films get, they always remains superficial. There’s always a naive optimism beneath it all that only the son of a billionaire could drum up.

É meio cômico que queiram reconhecer esse como um filme "que respira Brasil" (como vi alguém dizer) sendo que ele é feito num molde super estadunidense. Se não fosse a história real que o inspirou e os nomes dos personagens e locais, daria pra fingir que é só mais um drama americano qualquer. Além desse molde estadunidense, o maior problema pra mim é que ele é extremamente apelativo em vários momentos ao mesmo tempo que entrega um texto que chega ser covarde de tão apolítico. Não chega nem perto da dimensão do que foi a ditadura, não tem pulso pra lidar com uma tragédia dessa, é como se fosse uma "revolta" branda, que sabe-se lá por que($$?) se recusa a botar o quão monstruoso tudo foi. Se assumisse ser uma história sobre superação do luto com a ditadura apenas como pano de fundo, seria um filme 10x melhor, mas por algum motivo os envolvidos (e os fãs deles e do filme) querem com todas as forças colocar "Ainda Estou Aqui" como um dos projetos definitivos sobre a ditadura. Não é. Nem de longe. A Fernanda Torres no geral tá ótima e salva muito o filme de ser mais oco que já é (como na cena da sorveteria ou na da entrevista), mas ainda assim tem alguns momentos que derrapa feio na atuação (a cena dela gritando e batendo no vidro do carro é constrangedora). Selton Mello tá fofo numa primeira assistida, mas depois fica soando só meio besta e sem personalidade (como quase tudo que ele fez nos últimos anos, aliás). Quem sai por cima do elenco, além da Fernanda quando a direção pasteurizada do Walter não esmaga ela, é a Luiza Kosovski, que tem algumas das cenas mais fortes junto com a Torres. O final é algo quase estúpido. Podia ser lindo, mostrando como o fascismo não destruiu aquela família e blábláblá, mas o tom e, principalmente, a fotografia parecem mais uma propaganda de final de ano do itaú que qualquer outra coisa. A Fernanda Montenegro é uma das melhores atrizes do país? Sem dúvidas, mas aqui ela não empresta nem 5% do talento e do magnetismo dela, parece que só aceitou fazer por que a filha é a grande estrela e é dirigido por um amigo que lhe deu o seu melhor papel anos atrás. De pontos realmente muito positivos tem todo o desing de produção e a ambientação da casa dos Paiva, que é praticamente uma co-protagonista. Tudo ali soa vivo, autêntico, real. É uma pena que quase todo resto do filme seja tão plástico, formulaico, quadrado.

Obviamente le tenía que dar una oportunidad a I'm Still Here por todo el bombo que hubo desde que arrasó en los Óscar, pero ya cuando vi Central Station me di cuenta que el estilo de Walter Salles quizás no era para mí. La memoria es un tema difícil de tratar en el cine y a mí simplemente no me encajó el enfoque que tomaron aquí. Salles camina por el sendero obvio con las largas tomas en los lugares de tortura, los niños sufriendo por su padre... Aún así, siento que no se mete en el lodo lo suficiente para profundizar lo necesario en los personajes y en lo que significa para ellos lo que está pasando. Consigue que el espectador se implique en lo que ocurre con una puesta en escena directa, pero en lo personal me costó que me importaran sus personajes por la distancia que adopta el director al contar una historia real tan impactante.

La película narra los horrores de la dictadura brasileña sin caer en la moralina ni en el sentimentalismo. Al enfocarse en los aspectos humanos y el dolor de quienes nunca obtuvieron respuesta sobre la desaparición de sus seres queridos, el guion se vuelve más impactante a medida que avanza. Las actuaciones de los jóvenes actores son excelentes. Torres ofrece una actuación sutil y conmovedora en la que sus ojos transmiten más que mil palabras. Delgada y elegante. Lo que hace que este film sea aún más significativa, es su profunda conexión con lo que sucede en el mundo actual. Es un fuerte recordatorio de los peligros de que los gobiernos tengan demasiado poder y de por qué es tan importante proteger la democracia. No es solo una película, es una historia importante que todos deberían ver y comentar.

I respect what I’m Still Here (Ainda Estou Aqui) is trying to do but I honestly struggled to stay fully engaged. Clocking in at over two hours and twenty minutes, personally for me the pacing felt painfully slow. This easily could’ve been trimmed down to under two hours without losing its core message. Because of the heavy, distant pacing, I couldn't fully connect with the family or the emotional beats the way I wanted to. You can feel the weight and importance of the real-life history and Fernanda Torres turns in a grounded performance but for me it felt more like watching a historical documentary than a compelling narrative that hooked me.

Mi sono commossa più di una volta ma la parte finale mi ha lasciata davvero perplessa. Eunice è una sostenitrice dei diritti umani delle vittime della repressione politica, ha lottato per tantissimi anni della sua vita per la campagna per aprire i registri chiusi della dittatura militare e ha sostenuto i diritti dei popoli indigeni del Brasile, eppure, di tutto il suo lavoro, e tanto meno del genocidio avvenuto, non si vede niente nel film se non una scritta alla fine,parte in cui c’è una fievole volontà di uscire dalla vita privata di Eunice e denunciare gli orrori della dittatura.E lo fa anche pateticamente con la classica frase che invita a non ripetere gli stessi errori che mi sa di insensibile, considerando che di come il Brasile sia diventato una dittatura non lo tocca mai. Per questo mi pare che al film importi davvero di mostrare la dittatura solo negli effetti che ha avuto sulla classe media, e ancora più specificamente su una famiglia a dir poco presentata come perfetta. Porta avanti una debolissima rappresentazione della causa rivoluzionaria, in cui puccia solamente i mignolini nel momento in cui decide di svegliarsi a riguardo negli ultimi 10 minuti rimanenti, cosa davvero paradossale considerando la donna che fu Eunice. Per il resto, nonostante mi renda conto che la biografia della famiglia possa essere stata romanzata, la loro storia il regista l’ha narrata davvero bene.

I'm Still Here es un drama histórico sólido sobre la dictadura militar brasileña, pero creo que exige una conexión emocional con ese contexto que, al menos en mi caso, nunca terminó de aparecer. Entiendo perfectamente la importancia que tiene para Brasil recuperar esta historia y poner rostro a las víctimas de un régimen que persiguió, secuestró e hizo desaparecer a quienes consideraba una amenaza. Precisamente por eso se entiende el enorme reconocimiento que ha recibido: ganó el Óscar a la Mejor Película Internacional y el Goya a la Mejor Película Iberoamericana. La película funciona muy bien mostrando la lucha institucional de Eunice Paiva por mantener viva la memoria de su marido frente a un Estado que pretende borrar cualquier rastro de sus crímenes. Es un relato sobre la burocracia, la resistencia y la dignidad mucho más que sobre la violencia explícita de la dictadura. Sin embargo, no terminé de conectar con ella. El ritmo es muy pausado, la historia avanza lentamente y la sensación de impotencia acaba pesando más que el propio conflicto. Entiendo que esa sea precisamente la intención del director, pero personalmente esperaba una propuesta con un desarrollo más intenso o un conflicto narrativo que me atrapara más. No me parece una mala película; al contrario, está muy bien hecha y comprendo perfectamente su relevancia histórica y política. Simplemente creo que pertenece a esa categoría de películas impecables en su ejecución, pero que difícilmente recordaré dentro de unos años. Para mí se queda en un 3/5: buena, necesaria y respetable, pero sin llegar a emocionarme tanto como esperaba.

A forma que a casa dos Paiva parece possuir vida e sentimento é perceptível assim que o Rubens deixa a casa, um ambiente aconchegante se torna um ambiente frio, escuro e sombrio, além da perfeita atuação da Fernanda Torres que expressou perfeitamente o que qualquer ser humano sentiria acerca de tal situação A única reclamação para esse filme é como o filme se limita a escolhas feitas no filme que geram contradição. O problema do filme ser mais um filme que retrata a ditadura militar aos olhos da classe média alta, uma elite intelectual fragilizada durante esse período, não está propriamente no filme em si, o problema é a falta de retratamento de pessoas como a empregada dos Paiva durante a ditadura, a falta de histórias de quem não tinha uma casa grande à beira da praia O filme no geral é talvez o filme mais bem trabalhado de Salles, emocionante e como filme funciona perfeitamente e transmite todas as emoções que o filme quer que você tenha A cena da Eunice vendo uma família feliz na sorveteria é uma cena que molha minha visão somente ao pensar

روایت بین دو خط سیاسی و بازنمایی زندگی و جهان فراغ از آن گیر افتاده است به همین دلیل نه میتواند جامعه ای تحت سلطه استبداد بسازد و نه میتواند خانواده بسازدد، به خصوص خانواده متاثر از آسیب چنین جامعه ای! فیلم با جهان خانواده و با محوریت شخصیت اصلی یعنی (مادر خانه) آغاز میشود، جهانی که گه گاه اشاراتی به فضای سیاسی جامعه برزیل دارد اما تکیه بر خانواده ای و پرجمعیت که احتمالا قرار است اتفاقی باعث از هم پاشیدگی یا اسیب به ان میشود. اتفاقا نقطه عطف داستان یعنی گرفتار شدن روبنس سبب میشود که کارگردان به دلیل عدم انتخاب در زاویه نسبت به روایت خود باعث میگردد که روایت بلاتکلیف بماند و خانواداه ای که در ابتدای روایت به کشل نسبتاً خوبی در حال شکلگیری بود، شخصیت‌هایش تبدیل به جزیره‌هایی میگردند که تا پایان روایت نقطه اتصالی در آنها نمیتوان یافت. البته در نقطه عطف بزرگ یعنی در زمان که دستگیر شدن روبنس و به طبع آن اونیسی و دخترشان اندکی فضای فیلم که نگاه سیاسی در آن غالب است سعی دارد آن رعب و وحشت و بی‌منطقی حاکم را بسازد اما در آن موفق نیست. بعد از این است که روایت دچار افت معنا و فرم میشود و شخصیت‌های سرگردان (به خصوص فرعی مانند وکیل یا روزنامه‌نگاران و دوستان روبنس) باعث میگردد که اثرات سنگینی که میتواند چنین اتفاقی بر خانواده بگذارد مشاهده ننماییم. در نهایت روایت داستان در جایی که خانواده تصمیم به ترک و رفتن به سائوپائولو میگیرند پایان میپذیرد که همین نقطه نیز توانایی ساخت یک روایت تمام کمال را ندارد اما از نظر پایان بندی میتوانست نقطه مناسبی باشد. اما به دلیل وفادار بودن کارگردان به روایت اصلی که فیلم بر اساس آن ساخته شده فیلم ادامه میابد و از اینجاست که فیلم به شدت ضعیف و کاریکاتوری پیش میرود. ما ناگهان به 25 سال بعد منتقل میشویم، نه برای دیدن خانواده ای که اثرات این ماجرا را متحمل است، بلکه برای اینکه نامه گواهی فوت روبنس به دست اونیسی برسد و در فیلم ثبت گردد. عجیبتر اینکه باز هم 18 سال پیش میرویم و یک خانواده را میبینیم که هیچ بازتاب دراماتیک ندارند و تنها برای اینکه ما ناگهان اونیسی را در حال دیدن گزارشی از قهرمان بودن روبنس ببیند. این مخ آخر به این روایت ناقص و ضعیف است. البته نمی‌توان از سکانس‌های خوبی در ابتدای فیلم که مربوط به خانواده است صرفه نظر کرد، هرچند که نمی‌توان به فرزندان نزدیک شد به این دلیل که فیلم بیش از حد متکی به شخصیت اصلی (اونیسی) است و همان را هم ناقص می‌سازد. همچنین بازی خوب .. در نقش اونیسی نیز باعث شده که فیلم تحمل‌پذیرتر باشد. در مجموع روایتی ناقص و بی‌هدف که تکلیفش با خودش مشخص نیست، باعث می‌شود فیلم به یک فیلم متوسط تنزل پیدا کند.

Dieser Film hat mich an manchen Stellen tief berührt. Doch mein Rating variiert zu verschiedenen Zeitpunkten stark. Die Hauptdarstellerin und die Figur der Mutter sind für mich das Schönste gewesen - man sieht sie nicht in Selbstmitleid verfallen, sie ist unerschütterlich tapfer, radikal pragmatisch, strahlt Besonnenheit aus und dann diese rührende Zärtlichkeit ihrer Familie gegenüber - und zeitgleich sieht man ihr an, wie sie der Verlust des Mannes und dessen Umstände unwiderruflich gebrochen haben. Sie strahlt zum einen leise Hoffnung, Resilienz, aber zum anderen endlose Melancholie aus. Dieses Schauspiel verdient wirklich Aufmerksamkeit, Fernanda Torres ist unglaublich charismatisch. Zum Ende des zweiten Akts möchte ich dem Film somit gern vier Sterne geben. Aber in anderen Momenten verfällt der Film in Kitsch, wie im letzten Akt - das ist wirklich ärgerlich. Außerdem kratzt mir der Film zu sehr an der Oberfläche, ist unpolitisch und fokussiert sich zu sehr auf die Biografie des Einzelnen. Da würde ich doch am liebsten nur 2 1/2 Sterne geben aus reinem Trotz. So fühlt sich mein Fazit nicht ganz authentisch an. Dem hohem Averagerating kann ich mich nicht anschließen, für ein Meisterwerk halte ich den Film bei Weitem nicht. Very gripping true story! Very sickening too if I’m honest - dictatorships like that in Brazil are just disgusting the way they treat their people. Scary. Honestly thought this was heavily emotional - the acting across the board was top notch, and helped me feel every emotion on the board. Fernanda Torres shines in her role as Eunice; an absolute powerhouse performance. Loved Mikey Maddison in Anora, but this was the performance of the year for me. No doubts there. Shame she didn’t take it. Critics’ tastes never fail to baffle me. The first half of this film is one of the most gripping of 2024. Eyes glued to the screen, incredibly tight screenplay keeping me utterly hooked and invested in the characters, and a filmmaking style to invokes a proper real-life, yet nostalgic feeling in the first 30 minutes. I thought it was so important to showcase their day to day family life in the beginning of the film - it helps make the devastation feel all that more sudden and shocking! Unfortunately after the capture situation, i feel like the film loses its way a bit, the pacing slows down quite a bit, and the interesting plot slowly fizzles out, which is a shame, because the first half of the film was incredibly written and paced. That’s the problem with real life stories - they can only be as interesting as the actual story, unless you want to manipulate events that happen, which is never a good idea. So it’s almost hard to criticise the filmmaker for this, when there’s a lack of creative freedom when adapting a true story. This was a great film though - a must watch emotional tale of grief and heartbreak. It’s not without its fun opening half hour, but don’t expect thrills and joy after that mark, it’s all depressing from there. Truly harrowing story.

While it didn’t quite hit me as hard emotionally, I understand why this would be so devastating to so many people. Especially considering this all being real. As far as just as a film goes, I have 1 or 2 nitpicks that prevent me from loving it but it’s still great.

Goodness gracious, I get existential about the ability to authentically portray period in films as time, technology, and civilization moves on but movies like I'm Still Here give so much reassurance and strength whilst bravely dealing with crises of their own. To process an entire generation's worth of grief under dictatorial rule is not the goal of this film, but through a somewhat high-profile example that speaks to thousands of personal histories, this film is pretty exemplary. It shows how stark and banal the backslide into this type of brutal rule can and will look like. A nation always outnumbers its government but a combination of shocking brutality, public grandstanding, collusion with corporate interests, and hoarding of resources will depress the power of any individual or small group. It's quite scary to lose the power of criticism, the gumption to inspire change in your country, or the relative simplicity of alternate viewpoints under threat of sanction, capture, and/or murder. I'm Still Here explores these consequences mostly offscreen, putting in its place the shattering of an idealized household. This property on the beach becomes a visual metaphor for Brazil in microcosm as the tumult plays out. Incredibly dark forces threaten to ruin and re-contextualize the beautiful lands you call home and yet, there's nowhere else you'd rather be, with nothing to do but try and find peace. It is noble to stand up in face of these inhumane challenges but life can be so unfair. There is no guarantee of reward or recompense. If anything, the point of a journey like this is not to be persuaded, but to be well and truly broken. Everyone possesses a personal tolerance for such things. Bravery is taking yourself over the edge without much care as to the outcome, only that there is one. Dense, deep, emotional, I'm Still Here is no easy watch per se but it is a deeply informing and affecting one, driven by Fernanda Torres's incredible performance, as well as the film's immaculate capture of Brazil's view of the coup.

Not every tragedy has to be told on the biggest scale it can be. While hundreds were killed and disappeared during Brazil's military dictatorship, choosing to focus on one specific instance so that we can really come to love this family before it gets told apart makes it hit much harder. Stunning performances all around with a really great cameo by the legendary Fernanda Montenegro (best nonagenarian performance ever?). For whatever reason, I don't always love how it looks, especially the grittier second half, and thought the script sometimes could have done more showing less telling, but these are minor nitpicks. Powerful and important movie.

The film requires a fair amount of patience, especially at the beginning, as the story unfolds slowly. But the longer it goes on, the more it pays off. The performances are excellent, and it has one of the most emotionally powerful endings I can remember seeing in recent years. This isn’t a movie you put on to have a good time. It’s a film you watch knowing that what you’re about to see is a powerful true story, told and crafted with real care and quality.

Filme estrangeiro de uma história comovente, e que consegue quebrar a barreira cultural, em todo o mundo sentiu-se a mensagem que este filme quis transmitir, e mesmo perante as diferenças, várias comunidades que tiveram experiências semelhantes, identificaram-se

Es tan bella como dolorosa. La primera parte es una construcción fuertísima. Vemos a una familia perfecta, llena de amor, de sueños, con un sentido de comunidad inusitado del que todos quisiéramos formar parte. Y al mismo tiempo, sabes que algo malo va a pasar. Y mientras más amor hay, sabemos que más nos va a doler. Como en la realidad. Hay una anticipación terrible, palpable. Y luego sobre la memoria, y recordar con amor y no con dolor. La importancia de los recuerdos, y de preservarlos. Eso se nota muy claro con las fotografías y los videos que toman. Y me imagino que hay un comentario ahí sobre cómo los recuerdos se sienten diferentes al presente cuando muestran diferentes formatos. Pero me quedo con eso. Con que el amor no termina cuando la persona ya no está. Se cultiva, se crece. Con la importancia de recordar y de preservar la memoria, aunque duela, porque los seres queridos no se van hasta que los olvidamos.

Ainda Estou Aqui trás sensações fortes e vividas, impotência, insegurança, pavor... Mas é admirável o quanto Eunice se manteve forte e lutou por si, os filhos e o marido. Para mim, é um filme muito pessoal, tendo um bisavô que foi preso durante a ditadura e voltou para casa calado, coberto de marcas pelo corpo, e nunca contou as crueldades que passou na mão dos militares. Filme que me emocionou, marcando a história brasileira com um Oscar, e mostrando o terror da ditadura militar. Mesmo com o silêncio, Fernanda Montenegro conseguiu exressar uma dor tão sensível.

Quem não gostou não entende nada de história e diz que ditadura militar nunca existiu no Brasil. Esse filme é uma ótima representação do sofrimento de muitas pessoas que é ignorado até nós dias atuais. Pessoas foram torturadas por terem opiniões,posicionamentos ou estilos de vida diferentes,sem contar nos inúmeros casos de violência à pessoas negras,as quais sempre foram marginalizadas nesse país. Ainda estou aqui fala por essas pessoas,mostra uma historia real,mostra a dor de perder alguém e não saber onde essa pessoa está,a dor de não poder enterrar seu ente querido por nunca encontrar seu corpo. É um filme incrível que trouxe uma grande honra ao cinema brasileiro.

I thought a lot of the performances were quite bad, Chastain and Caine especially, I thought Hathaway and the two children were quite good. Damon's performance was really good, him emerging from cryosleep was a haunting high point for the film but the awful scuffle and monologue he delivers afterwords is a cavernous low and he proceeds to fall apart as a character. I was prepared to give this film 2 stars but the awful, self-ashamed "eureka!" delivered by Chastain in the film's climax singlehandedly tanked that. I am actually appalled that this film has the reputation that it does, I guess I wish I saw what everyone else does in it.

Felt it necessary to rewatch since it’d been a decade. Despite its best efforts to conform to a more transcendent cinematic language, drawing from 2001 and other monuments of modernist cinema, the film is fundamentally incapable of embodying that language because of its ideological hostility to the very nature of art. Where 2001 embraces mystery, ambiguity, and the limits of human understanding, Interstellar cannot help but reduce everything to a problem awaiting calculation. The film reeks of the resurgent scientific arrogance that defined much of the 2010s, the kind embodied by Dawkins and his contemporaries. And Elon Musk now a testament of its logical conclusion. It carries the self-assured belief that scientific reasoning and human computation alone are sufficient to save humanity from the very crises those same forces helped create. Even the film’s apparent concession to the irrational, love, is ultimately folded back into the logic of quantification. And thus, even the very medium used to tell this story becomes a means to a self-defeating end. The older I get, the more deeply I believe that the arts are our greatest means of approaching transcendence. Art is how we encounter the sacred, how we gesture toward truths that words, logic, and reason can only circle. To use cinema in service of an ideology that insists every mystery must ultimately be rendered calculable is to undermine the very essence of the art form itself. A truly evil film.

This film is incredibly overrated. I had high expectations coming into this film; due to all the praise online deeming it a ‘masterpiece’ and one of the ‘greatest movies of all time’,but I was left thoroughly disappointed. The dialogue in this film is awful in many instances, the prime example being  “love transcends space and time” which is an incredibly idiotic line coming from a NASA scientist, and feels incredibly out of place in a sci-fi drama. Another problem with this film is the lack of character development specifically with characters like Amelia Brand and the other crew members, I had no connection or care for any of these characters, which led to many of the scenes that were intended to be hard-hitting and emotional not resonating with me in the way that they should have. I feel that the writing in this film drags this film down heavily and the conclusion to this film made no sense- Cooper spends the whole movie trying to get back to his daughter just for him to leave again within 30 seconds of finally reuniting. However, this film has a some great qualities such as the breathtaking visuals and the incredible score and a few fantastic moments and great performances fromMatthew McConaughey who gives an awe-inspiring performance as Cooper and the actress who played young murph (who is superb in this film). Despite the lousy dialogue and some of the terrible moments in this film, this is still a decent watch but is no where near as great as people are describing it.

I finally got around to watching every white dude's favorite film, and I really wanted to love it based on all the great things I had heard. However, I was bored the entire movie, and kept predicting what was going to happen next. The only two things I didn't predict were Dr. Mann turning on them & trying to kill Cooper, & the ending. Going into it, I literally said, "Let me guess, all the people on the mission are going to die except for Cooper & Brand." I was right. I didn't see the point of him leaving in the first place. I get that he wanted to save his family, but it ultimately seemed like a selfish decision to get to leave the planet you know is dying & your kids behind with it. He had no clue how many years it was going to be until he returned, or if he would even return at all. He left way too quickly in the beginning and left his daughter there sobbing (stupid). His son didn't even really seem to care that his dad left, and then at the end of the movie, Cooper doesn't even try to find his son?! What?? It's like he only cared about his daughter towards the end of the film. I wished that during the end they would show Murph at different ages trying to figure out what the gravity meant, but they clearly didn't want to hire another actor (lazy). I thought that the "gravity has the same properties as time" thing was dumb. If the wormhole was created by "them" in the future, how did they even get there in the first place to create the wormhole? I really didn't want to be a hater, but this film was just bad. The one thing I did like was the score; Hans always does a spectacular job. Overall, I have to give it a 2/5.

Nolan joue avec les lois de la physique que son équipe de production lui a rapporté, au détriment de la vraisemblance et d'une certaine cohérence interne au film. Le résultat produit laisse le souffle coupé la première fois qu'on le voit tant ce concept psyché-SF de l'envers du trou noir est nouveau, mais résiste difficilement à plusieurs visionnages, soit au passage du temps... Boasts itself as both the most popular and most viewed film on this very platform as of this writing; I was likely going to stumble into it sooner or later, but of course since The Odyssey is the current hot (and somewhat contested despite what scores on here and IMDB would indicate otherwise) new thing, I just had to dive back into Christopher Nolan once more. Do I think this is any good? …Sort of? The production design is well crafted, colour grading is decent, the space stuff itself seems to have been thoroughly researched, and I can’t deny the score is well composed. However, like plenty of these Nolen directed flicks, it’s the story which I struggle to emotionally connect with. Not for lack of trying however, I just don’t feel that emotional spark others seem to with this guy’s works. Also, I think I just prefer 2002: A Space Odyseey as far as space travel films go, that one got weirder with it decades earlier and leaves further unanswered questions in its wake. Also, the World of Tomorrow shorts emotionally connect with me way more while also balancing a combination of weirdness and absurdity for that matter. I think I know what I’m looking for in Sci Fi at this point, and I don’t think this film is quite it with its attempts to be sentimental and tear jerking. This has its moments, don’t get me wrong, but they’re a bit too spread out for me across the almost three hour runtime for me to get into it fully. At least I can say I watched it and got something out of it.

Expectations were definitely met. I've been putting off this watch for a while for whatever reason. Maybe because I thought I wouldn't like it as much as I thought I would? But no, it's pretty fucking good and the accolades are well deserved. Visually, it's beautiful, and it uses a ton of stunning imagery to show that. It has some very, very awesome sequences with some of the most stunning visuals I've ever seen in a film. The score is phenomenal and evokes just as much emotion in every scene as the looks. It's a great narrative, and the emotional arc really hit me. At the same time, it shows Nolan's biggest weakness: exposition. It's a tell-more-than-show kind of thing. But because of how good it looks, I'm inclined to let most of it slide. I just wish Nolan would have allowed for some of the stuff to have an ambiguous element. To leave some space for what doesn't need to be explained. Because the sciencey stuff can still be reallyyy cool without having to tell the viewer everything about it. Still, such a great film though and definitely worth the watch.
